text: Who knew St. Louis could be so hip? The Grove area has it going on these days - first a giant sign that now lets you know exactly the name of their 'hood, now a bicycle-friendly bar! Seems like our fair city is starting to keep up with the rest of the world... Stopped in Handle Bar for a quick drink with a gal pal the other night. It was empty inside, but I got here right at 5 pm. In addition to cheap drafts during happy hour, they also have a "Bartender's Special" - that night it was Guinness. I wasn't having it, but I know we have some yelpers out there who are fans. I tried the Six Row Whale - MAN! That's some good beer! Had I not had other plans that night, I would have been content sitting at that bar and drinking myself silly with Whale beer. My companion and I tried to order an appetizer, but the kitchen wasn't opening until 6. And about the time we were packing up, our cute little bartender brought us a plate of hummus. I felt terrible 'case we didn't have time to eat it, but I'm thinking she was able to put it to good use (i.e., her tummy). Come check out this cool bar! It's in a great STL area, the drinks are cheap, the staff is nice and they care about the planet. What more do you want, people?

text: Since I moved here about a year ago, Marathon Grill suffered through two shootings at the adjacent movie theatre along with a couple rowdy bar fights at Mar Bar, so I pretty much avoided that entire area altogether. Yesterday, my beloved and I decided to eat dinner there before watching Predator II because it was sweltering hot, we were bored and it was the closest entertainment-related venue to our place. I guess we decided to put the shootings behind us and risk it. Either way, I'm glad I stopped by because it happened to be University City Dining Days so we each got a substantial soup, entree and dessert for $15. So onto the food itself: Appetizer: Vegetarian Chili Not the most flavorful chili I've ever tasted (and I totally believe in flavorful vegetarian food now since I can actually cook it myself, dammit!) and there was a huge glob of sour cream inside which I had to work around. The Premium saltines made it better. Entree: Pappardelle with Shiitake & Cremini Pappardelle is like my pizza--I'll even eat the bad ones. There were some burnt pieces of mushroom in there that somehow made it taste better. Overall it was a decent dish. I'm glad they didn't put too much sauce on it as some low-end Italian places tend to do. Dessert: Banana Bread Pudding with Ice Cream This is actually just a piece of dry banana bread with a scoop of vanilla ice cream on it--not real bread pudding. The ice cream had caramel drizzle on it that fell off like pieces of macaroni on a kid's art project. Drinks: I ordered a pineapple juice with coconut rum and it was good! Not that anybody can really mess that up, though... at least I hope. Service: The waitresses that we interacted with were all extremely friendly and helpful. However, it took a bit to find someone when we needed something and neither the soups or dessert came with a spoon which we had to wait for. All in all, we didn't get shot. I guess that makes this dinner a success.
label: NEG

text: You can't spell "hype" without Shiroi Hana! -------------- Before I begin, I have to apologize to Stephanie Y (3/31/10) - she was spot on with her review of this place! Either I'm a sushi snob, or too many people have unrefined palates. Or both. After reading so many good reviews about this place, we decided to come here for dinner. We split an order of the hard core sushi combo, tempura, and a spider roll. - Tempura: fried very well. Dipping sauce had a touch of ginger. - Spider roll: average. Too much lettuce, which in my opinion has no role in ...a role. - Hard core sushi combo: they ran out of surf clam, and so I asked to substitute for an additional piece of uni. The uni was VERY DISAPPOINTING, and had obviously been sitting out for too long. It was half melted before it arrived, and it had no creamy, "umami" sweetness (it tasted salty, which reflects BAD uni). The overall fish quality was mediocre, and MUCH better fish can be had at 3rd & Chestnut, 2nd & South, etc etc... Let's not even mention the poor wrapping job on the salmon roe sushi (see my pic) It got the second star only because of doting service. I bet the reason why this place gets massive grade inflation is that people review their the cooked items. I thought this was a sushi restaurant, not a Yakitori restaurant?!

text: Really, I don't get what all the hype is about. I tried a few of their very expensive cup cakes and honestly, they are no better here then anywhere else I've been recently. I will say that they do have a very extensive and unique selection. I tried two different flavors - some kind of peanut butter chocolate which sounded much more exciting then it was and the other was more traditional vanilla cake. I was really anticipating my visit because I heard so many good things about these cupcakes, but they would need to bring the prices way down to get me back in there. The staff were friendly and helpful. The atmosphere of the store is perfect for their product and they seem to really care about what they are doing. Note: This is an update to my review. text: Executive summary: Really yummy pulled pork and cole slaw at a shack, everything else fine, but not as stand out as those two. This shack has the added appeal of being right next door to the diviest looking dive bar that I have ever seen maybe. You can smell the stench of sour beer wafting by now and then on a weekend lunch. OK, maybe that is one downside of the outdoor only seating, but it sure adds to the authentic feel of the place. We got a pulled pork and a beef at the cashiers recommendation. The pork was delicious, the beef was good, but compared to the pork it just couldn't stand up, not much could have really, that pork was really something. The cole slaw was great as were the black eyed peas. The mashed potatoes were fine but compared to the buttermilk mashed potatoes at Swetts they just lacked flavor. The corn bread pancakes and grilled pickle were fine too but not nearly as outstanding as the pulled pork. They only had one piece of peach cobbler left and it did not look so good, so we had the blackberry cobbler and it was good too, but again, after that pork, everything else just seemed good. Interesting side note: according to our cashier, something like 5 of the 8 people that work there are now vegetarians after working there for a couple years. Too much of a good thing I guess!!! hahahaha

text: I want to go out on a limb here and say that the Regency Café is the keystone, centerpiece, starting block, whatever clever saying you want to use here, to the Lansdowne renaissance that has started happening these past couple of years. Located in the heart of downtown Lansdowne, the Regency seems like it came straight outta University City, Northern Liberties or some other hip, gentrified spot in Philly. The sandwiches are tasty and the drinks definitely quench your thirst. It is the perfect place to stop in after you catch a movie at the art-house next-door. If you live in Lansdowne, take advantage of walking or riding your bicycle there. If you are coming by car, there is a parking lot conveniently located across the street, not to mention the train station two or three blocks down the road. When Lansdowne turns into the next hotspot to live in Delaware County, they should thank the Regency Café for getting the ball rolling.

text: I lucked into the bargain of the century when i got a room at The Royal Sonesta. The rooms are spacious and well appointed. Internet access was good, and moving around inside the hotel was easy. There are plenty of shops, lounges and restaurants without even having to leave the front door. I wandered through a lot of other hotels in the area, and I really felt like I had found the best one based on lobby and shops, the lounges, and my contact with the employees. If I go back, I'll always check this hotel first. If I have the chance, I'll stay there in a heartbeat.

The philadelphia roll had bright green avocado and thick, but not overpowering chunks of cream cheese. And the spicy tuna had nice chunks of fresh meat, rather than minced pieces of who-knows-how-old mystery flesh. It was actually more food than I thought it would be, and kept me from following through on my plan to get frozen yogurt from up the street. I definitely want to go back to try the Korean lunch menu, and for dinner.

text: What a great surprise for my first visit to Indy! I popped onto Yelp trying to figure out what to grab for dinner after a rough day of travel and work. Staying by the airport, there wasn't a ton around... Luckily for me, Bosphorus was only 12-15 minutes away. Just S.E. of downtown, the restaurant is a small 15 table or so business run by a nice family. At 7PM on a Wednesday there were a half dozen parties when I got there. I decided to have lentil soup, Doner, and rice pudding with Efez Dark Turkish beer and Turkish coffee to wash things down. I thought the bright yellow lentil soup was good although could have used a pinch more seasoning for me. The Doner was flat out awesome! As a frequent traveler to Germany, I used to eat a lot of Doner and struggle to find it in the states. For the uninitiated, Doner is seasoned lamb shaved from a rotating roasting spit. Bosphorus served it with a fresh green salad, vegetables, sauce and pita. The Efez Dark was a nice beer that I would best refer to as Turkey's answer to Negro Modelo. The second one was even better than the first. I questioned whether or not I wanted to spring for dessert but the thought of Turkish coffee and rice pudding was too much to resist. I am SO glad I did; the rice pudding was a perfect consistency and flavor. Each spoonful of the large bowl was "heaven". And the coffee was "black as midnight" and "strong as love". The atmosphere was casual yet nice enough to use for a birthday party (which was the reason two tables were there). The service was attentive and pleasant without being smothering, which can sometimes be the downside of being a party of one. At the end of the day, if you like middle Eastern cuisine, you can't go wrong with Bosphorus. Great stuff!
label: POS

text: Several years back, I visited here, had Hasenpfeffer and was delighted! It was evening, and the band playing was reminiscent of old days overseas. Some time later, I talked my family into dropping in for lunch during the return trip of our vacation. The service was abysmal, and the food not quite on par with the service. I've never seen nor heard of a Schnitzel made with the type of coating one finds on Long John Silver's fish...and burnt, to boot. The waiter, whom I longed to smack, did at least warn me not to expect much if I ordered German. I thought, well, it might still be OKAY. I thought WRONG, and "smackable waitguy" was understating. Fortunately, I substituted a somewhat-less-burnt, better-than-nothing Wurst. Those bestowing multiple stars for this joint are either relatives, awed by décor, or have never tasted authentic German cooking. Once leaving here, they STILL haven't. I've since warned others away, and won't return. They may have improved since, but I'm going to try all of the other Nashville German restaurants, instead. I've had better German food in Chicago, New York, Alabama, Georgia, St. Louis, Santa Barbara, and on and on and on. And it doesn't come near anything in Europe, not even remotely. So I guess, in retrospect, I've had better German food everywhere, including that I cook myself, which I'd rather. What are people thinking? It's the Werst Haus.

text: Chuy's is one large room with a bar on the side. It is very open, one wall is lined with booths and the remaining room is scattered with tables. They also have outdoor seating which is sectioned off from the busy Speedway street. Chuy's is not a restaurant! It is a bar with bar food. The bar food is disgusting. They have "Mexican" food items like tacos, burritos and fajitas, but most of their bar food items are fish and chicken. The baja sauce that came with my fish taco was pink. Fish taco sauce is supposed to be white, and salsa is supposed to come on fish tacos, so maybe the pink sauce is a mixture of the two? But the pink sauce didn't taste like salsa. Don't get me wrong, it was good, not as good as fish taco sauce that I stir up in my kitchen, but good. Er, decent. The garlic bread comes with cheese on top, which can be amazing if done right, but here it tastes like the bread sits out all day and the cheese turns into plastic before they serve it to you. If you would like a beer and don't mind a loud-yet-not-loud-enough bar atmosphere then come here because they have a complimentary chip and salsa counter. If this establishment would like more stars it needs to change its name from "Chuy's Baja Broiler" to "Chuy's Bar with a few bar food items that give people headaches."

text: I have to preface this review by saying I know absolutely nothing about Korean food and Kim's was my first and only "real" Korean BBQ experience. That said, I can't say enough good things about Kim's. The food is delicious, the service is great, the prices are right.... it's a top-notch joint. The first time I came, I ordered dolsot bibimbop, which I've had before at another Korean place my friends brought me to (read: I was playing it safe). I noticed the big charcoal pit in the middle of my table and I was intrigued. Next visit, I returned with a cadre of 6 people, and ordered two orders of the beef, one spicy, one regular. Two orders ended up being plenty, and we had a blast cooking our meat on the charcoal grill. Yes, that's right, you cook it yourself at your table. The staff bring you various side dishes, most of which I couldn't identify but all tasted great, and a couple types of toppings for the meat. The aromas of the cooking beef are just wonderful. And the flavor is mind blowing. It's like hibachi, kinda, but you do it yourself instead of having a show. The prices are very reasonable. Not cheap, but less than what you might expect for the type of experience, amount of food, and overall quality of what you're getting. And at the end, a delicious cup of complimentary ginger tea. And again, all served by helpful, friendly staff (although their English is not so great). Can't recommend Kim's enough for an awesome Korean BBQ experience.

One note to the management, they might want to work on the ventilation hoods in the kitchen, since the dining room was being smoked out. text: I keep wanting to call this place, 'Awful Awfuls', but it's not - that's the name of the signature burger! On 12/15, my friend treated me to dinner for my birthday, and this is what I asked for - sometimes I just want a good burger and fries, and the Awful Awful is almost always it; the only other place that comes close for me is Juicy's on Wells Ave. No wait to order, and we sat at the counter. There are some small tables outside of the diner as well. (To echo M.B.'s review, if you're a neat freak/uptight/upper class, the counter, and probably the tables, are not for you). I watched their preparation so I could see if there was something I could add at home to get closer to this taste. The only obvious thing was a lot of salt/seasoning added while the burger is on the grill. In under 10 minutes our order was served. This evening, the Awful Awful met my high expectations. The buns are toasted on the grill, then piled high with the burger with cheese, fresh lettuce, tomato, red onion, and dressing. It's so big, it's too much to bite into, so I edited out half of a head of lettuce. (j/k - but I should have edited out some onion too, because I was tasting that for hours afterwards.) The Awful Awful is served in a basket on top of a HEAP of french fries - like 2 large potatoes worth! I think when I first came here many years ago, the fries were fatter. Today they are more like shoestrings, maybe because they cook faster that way. The burger and fries had the savory taste I was craving, and in the 40 minutes we were here, there were another 10 walk up orders, all of them for an Awful Awful (or 2). While my November take-out order was not as tasty, I was glad I came back here for this evening.

It came with a side of hummus, the traditional tomato/cucumber chutney and of course rice. Everything had a distinctive flavor which made it a pleasure to mix stuff together. We finished off the meal with a hookah of golden apple flavored tobacco. The location really lends itself to relax and people watch while you enjoy the hookah. You can focus on the hipsters at the Last Drop or the occasional freakshow that stumbles out of Dirty Frank's. text: I'm going to be honest up front. I'm a bit of a sushi snob. My boyfriend would say I'm a HUGE sushi snob -- and I suppose he's right. So when a friend suggested we go to Blue Ocean Sushi for 'all you can eat sushi', I was a little skeptical. All you can eat sushi? For less than 30 bucks? Hmm. The mantra 'you get what you pay for' kept cycling through my head. I had visions of me crouched over a toilet at 2am, spewing up bad sushi. But...I can't resist sushi (or maybe I'm just a good friend?), so I braced myself for the worst and went along. The place is in a pretty nondescript building, across from the Delmar Lounge. It shares it's space with 609. The atmosphere left a LOT to be desired. I felt like I was in a warehouse. Concrete floors and everything. Hmm. It was warm and smelled of smoke. Ugh. It was too late for me to back out now! Like other yelpers have already mentioned, there are three tiers of all you can eat. I went with tier 2, which ran me about 24.99 for dinner. It allowed me to order anything in tier 2, or anything in tier 1. Not bad. Our waitress was cordial, but seemed to rush us along the entire night. Over the course of the evening, I had a few bowls of miso soup, eel nigiri, salmon nigiri, a eel avocado roll, crab rangoon, and albacore nigiri. That's a LOT of sushi. I did the math, and I DEFINITELY got my money's worth. But the important question -- was it good? Well...it was just OKAY. The eel nigiri was tasty (but really...it's pretty hard to fuck that up), the miso soup was average, and the eel avocado roll was good. The albacore was tasty, and the crab rangoon was AMAZING. But the salmon nigiri? Not fresh. Not fresh at all. In fact, although most things I tried were tasty, 'not fresh' was the theme of the night. I was too afraid to try interesting sounding nigiri pieces, for fear of food poisoning. Not a good feeling to have when dining out! It's saying a lot when the highlight of the meal was the crab rangoon. AT A SUSHI PLACE. To be honest, I don't know if I'd come back. The sushi was just a step above the stuff you can buy at the grocery store at the sushi counter. I'm more than willing to pay a few bucks more at Wasabi or any number of other sushi places in St. Louis for decent fish and peace of mind. Sorry, Blue Ocean. You just didn't do it for me. I might come back and give it one more shot. Maybe. MAYBE.

text: According to my parents the Sansom St. Oyster House is a Philadelphia institution, and it recently re-opened after extensive renovations. I came here for an early dinner to take advantage of the happy hour 'Buck-a-shuck' special. It's quite a deal - a select oyster (the Wild Blue Points on my night) were $1 if you sit at the bar or around the large raw bar, and one of the draft beers is $3. Its a great after work deal! The interior is really cool, a very modern take on an old time oyster bar - the extra wide white marble bar is very classic, and there is plenty of space to talk with friends and make new ones. The oyster selection is mostly from the mid-Atlantic / New England area, but there were one or two from Washington State and Oregon as well. Even the regular prices are quite reasonable at 2.25 to 2.75 for most varieties. I'll definitely be back!

I would suggest getting the gyoza (dumplings) or edamame for an appetizer. I would also suggest trying their martinis. While normally they are around $7 a pop for a martini, if you go on Monday nights, they are only $4. I usually get either the sake waterfall, the sake razz, the jade, the angel on acid, and the key lime martini. All of which are deliciously strong. And to top it all off, there is karaoke on Mondays. text: Again, another groupon purchase for me. I met my husband here for lunch one day, and it was pretty disappointing. I was shocked that they didn't have some sort of a lunch menu in such a busy business area. We both ordered a cup of Hot & Sour soup ($3) and a roll (Rainbow & El Camino). The Hot & Sour soup was interesting. It had great spice to it, but they put quartered raw button mushrooms in it and raw green onion slices. Don't get me wrong, I love fresh ingredients, but it really doesn't do anything for the soup. It just seemed like a cheap way to bulk up a tiny $3 cup of soup. Both the rolls were pretty bland. The fish and avocado on the rainbow roll was flavorless (but then again, it was November in a landlocked state, so that probably expected). The El Camino roll, despite the ingredients, lacked flavor too. I was expecting a lot since it had cilantro, peppers, and lime juice, but it was truly lackluster. Also, it had a "sprinkling" of sesame oil on it, and the sesame oil tasted old. (My husband thought I was nuts when I said this, but sesame oil ages quickly. If you ever cook with it, you can identify this.) And the service? Slow. Very, very slow. It took an insane amount of time to get two bowls of soup and two rolls (that required no cooking). Unfortunately we'll be going back since I have two more Groupons to burn, but I think we'll try the thai next time.

text: Stella Mare's is one of those places that has the potential to be the backdrop to a magically romantic evening. Stepping through the front door after dusk is like stepping into a completely different world of romance and luxury. The service is what you would expect of a restaurant in this price range, and the ambiance is worth the price of admission as well. The building itself is a unique design for a restaurant. Cozy dining rooms seem to be tucked behind one and other. My date and I were seated in the atrium area (which I'd highly suggest if you go at night). The entire room was candle-lit with only the night sky above us. I must admit that this is one of those times when the atmosphere might have made ordinary food taste extraordinary, however, the cuisine matches the entire scene. While everything I've tried is killer, the lobster bisque is the best I've ever had. This is more an event than a dinner. A good date or friend is key. But make sure you take your time and soak it all in, because its these sorts of places that make dining both tasty and meaningful.

text: The tables have little buttons that summon a server. These buttons are akin to those on an airplane, used to call the flight attendant. When pressed, a small chime is heard and a server will come and see what you want. I don't usually curse in my reviews, but I fucking love this. Everyone should do this everywhere. Yes, I understand that a good server should be checking up on you to make sure you have everything at regular intervals, but what if my demands don't come at regular intervals? What if my demand involves getting a paper towel quickly because my nose is runny due to consumption of really spicy food? What then hotshot? Wait until my server checks on me at the regular interval or hit the button that brings him or her over more quickly? I don't even have to make eye contact or wave. Bam. Button. Technology improves everything. I always say that efficiency is the most important human emotion and this feature appeals to that emotion greatly. Soft tofu really kicks ass. It basically boils down to tofu soup in a spicy broth with tofu, meat, kimchee, or whatever else you want in it. I had the opportunity to try seafood soft tofu and beef/kimchee soft tofu. I loved both but if I went back, I'd have to edge towards the beef/kimchee slightly above the seafood. This may have to do with the fact that pulling the prawn's head and skin off with my fingers was stressful because the prawn was very hot when I was doing this. I have very little patience when it comes to food and I frequently burn myself if things are served very hot because I have NO SELF CONTROL when it comes to something delicious. The best example of this is my habit of ordering iced coffee beverages, not because I really like it cold but because I want to prevent myself from burning myself...This topic applies to Jong Ka Jib Soft Tofu Restaurant because the soup is served at an extremely high temperature and I decided to use my tongue to cool off each glorious spoonful. This place is awesome. The price makes it double awesome. The food makes it triple awesome. The unique nature of the restaurant and server buttons make it quadruple awesome. Get your soft tofu super spicy. On the action-movie-parallel-satisfaction-scale, this establishment is my image of how great The Expendables should be. I haven't seen it but I don't think I should, as my expectations are impossibly high.

text: A friday night - and we were the only ones in the place for no less than 45 minutes. Service started off pretty good. Immediate offering of menu as we were seated. Waitress explained the menu. They had no bartender...so we switched to wine and a soft drink. We attempted to order Jamon Crudo y Muzarella con Rusa (Sliced Prosciutto and Mozzarella with Rusa Salad) waitress suggested we try the Empanadas - De Carne (Stuffed Beef Pastry) De pollo (Stuffed Chicken Pastry) De Jamón y. They were enjoyable. The main course was a whole other story. Vacio - 14 Oz. Bottom Sirloin flap steak* was ordered medium rare. It came out "blue" - just barely warm and very rare. A scoop of potatoes sat on the plate like displaced ice cream. The veggies were unremarkable in every way... not even a hint of seasoning. And there also sat a small heap of iceberg lettuce that was seemed to have no reason to be there. He ate the steak because he is okay with rare, but he did say multiple times that the quality of the cut was not a steak that he would normal want to eat rare. The entire dish as lacking of any interesting flavors or texture. Agnolotis - Pasta filled with ricotta, ham and almonds with tomato sauce. Their pasta is homemade, but they should really consider purchasing it... this pasta was either poorly made or over cooked... it was like paste, not pasta. The content was mush. The entire dish was all of the same texture (how is that possible with almonds???) it was reminiscent of eating oatmeal... just a blob. And the flavors were all of the same profile... I ended up pulling a couple of my partners green and red peppers from his plate and eating them within the dish to at least add one other layer of texture and flavor. The waitress did ask us how everything was almost immediately as the food was served... we had hardly had time to taste and check everything. We never saw her again until well after we had given up on the food. She missed an opportunity to get my friend another glass of wine, which would have been nice since it was gone by the middle of the meal. My soft drink was also gone half way through the meal.. we were darn glad that they had water on the table because that is the only way I was going to be able to choke my meal down without the help of a drink. We were going to try a dessert - in hopes that maybe it would be better than our meal. It was our attempt to leave after at least having a nice dessert. But after waiting and waiting and waiting for the waitress, we were only at that point interested in leaving. The environment was pretty. The music was entertaining for a while, but you can only listen to so many tango songs before you want to start tangoing your food up. It was too loud for the non crowded restaurant. and the tempo of the tango can actually be rather negative while trying to digest. Would be go back? Nope. Flavors are boring. Skill is lacking in prep of food and the service is sub par. Would we recommend to friends? Nope. I would hate to be responsible for someone else to go there and have a bad experience. Please excuse me now... I have to go burp up this blob of pasta goo just sitting in my tummy.

text: It's my first time: both on Yelp, and at Leila's, so go easy on me... When the storefront at the corner of 13th and Pine went vacant (Wasabi House moved to Camac & Pine), I was curious to see what would come of it. When the sign advertising middle eastern cuisine (and hookah bar!) was placed in the window, I made a mental note to support the new neighbors in my hood. However, it took a few months until the mood struck. I'm SO glad it finally did. When the bf and I entered the place, it was a bit ambiguous whether we were supposed to seat ourselves or wait for someone to assist. A few seconds into our confusion, we were greeted warmly by a man who seemed to be cook and waiter (and possibly owner?). He encouraged us to sit wherever we'd like, "we're very casual here." He was instantly likable, and his charm set the tone for a great evening out. Simply put, the food was amazing. We ordered too much of it, but it was just... so... good: a maza platter (a sampler of sorts) with tabouleh, hummus, baba ganoush, fatoush, pita, grape leaves (oh so spectacular grape leaves), feta and olives, tomatoes... and who knows, I probably left something out. The food just kept coming--and THAT was just the appetizer! I had a falafel platter on top of that (which I didn't realize also came with the tabouleh and hummus I was craving); the bf had what he described as a "perfectly cooked shwarma platter"--and he's picky, having lived in the middle east for a time. I had a milk, banana & honey smoothie. Admittedly, this sweet drink might seem like a strange addition to the garlic & herb mix that was my dinner, but it was a nice balance nonetheless. The value is exceptional--I think part of the reason why we ordered so much food is because we expected less of it, based on the prices (dear Leila Cafe: please don't change this--it's yet another reason to love you). Why four stars? Because Leila Cafe has the mixed honor / curse as my first Yelp, so I want to hold back a bit. I definitely expect this neighborhood cafe to be a regular in my rotation. And I know that I can always add the star that it probably already deserves.

I do want to insert a brief disclaimer that I prefer my physical practice to have an organic flow, something challenging enough I can just lose my thoughts in because I am so intimately focused on breath and movement. We didn't actually get onto our feet until 25 mins. into the class, which kind of felt like a waste of time. Eddie went into numerous, and I mean NUMEROUS stories - all of a very esoteric and nonsensical nature. Look, I totally get a narrative to start a class to draw a theme or focus for a deeper connection to the practice but after 10+ stories, I just found myself more irritated than inspired in any way. I do want to admit that I teach as well, so as an instructor I might be slightly more observant than others when it comes to sequencing. We only flowed through a handful of postures and my pet peeve is when an instructor forgets a very integral pose. The kind that when they forget my body literally feels crooked. If you can't remember your sequence of 10 poses - maybe less stories. I also prefer to have a balanced practice. Standing poses, twists, backbends, hip openers and maybe an inversion if possible. In a 90 min. class I got the first two. While I respectably offer that Eddie's style may appeal to a certain type of student, I know that is not me. I used to think that all yoga is good yoga, and it is very, very rare that I leave a class feeling worse than when I stepped onto my mat.....I guess there is a first time for everything.

It's seasoned pork sauteed with chorizo and pineapple on a soft corn tortilla with red onion and cilantro (usually). Any taqueria on Cherokee will do this taco well. Unfortunately, not Tower Tacos. I don't understand... they used to make these great!! I don't know what the meat was seasoned with and white onion? This is not an eastern European restaurant... That onion completely overpowered any sweetness or flavor that the taco could have had. $23 later and no chips were placed in the bag to go with our guacamole and meal. Twer Tacos needs to get back to the basics. Lose the Russian food, unless you are opening a "Tower Stuffed Peppers" restaurant and focus on good, solid Mexican food with fresh, quality ingredients. When ours arrived the beautiful presentation and our moans of pleasure caused two other tables to order it immediately. We ordered delicious Spaghetti alla Carbonara as an appetizer and prepared for the entrees. The entrees are limited at the Sycamore and change frequently. It's important to check the website. The wife enjoyed Seared Duck Magret and I devoured Red Wine Braised Beef Short Ribs. This is new American cuisine at its finest! We finished the meal with the wife's favorite desert; Tiramisu. Our evening included mixers for four drinks, Farmer's Plate, one appetizer, two entrees and one desert. We were pleasantly satiated and the tab was a very reasonable $108. We will definitely be back!

text: Travel to Tampa on business pretty frequently and have hit a lot of great dining spots (as you can see from past reviews!). After many heavy and high calorie meals, my vendor in Tampa took me to Seasons 52. The concept is that nothing on the menu is above 475 calories. This means you can share an appetizer, have a fresh salad, and an entree and not feel guilty. The menu is somewhat limited, but there are constant changing specials each week. Have now been there twice with large groups and everyone was loving their dinner. I enjoyed the shrimp pasta on my first visit and scallops on the second. Great spinach salad and little mini desserts that satisfied the sweet tooth. Service was excellent, wine list was great, and they let you sample some wines when deciding. Overall - two thumbs up and no need to unbutton that top button!

text: I'm on a roll lately. Five stars to Gold Club, with a two star average. Two stars for Modern Eye, with a five star average. Annnnd now two stars for Desi Chaat House which has a glowing five star average. Having recently discovered my taste for Indian food (discounting one meal that I ate before the Phish concert that I wanted to throw up later in the night due to exhaustion), I have been dying to try Desi Chaat House. I like crispy, I like street food, I like new things, and this place has had rave reviews, including both of my trusty Philly food resources: City Paper's Meal Ticket AND Phoodie. But I wasn't blown away. At all. The "facebook fan" drink I received was by far the highlight of the meal. It was fresh tasting and mangoey and bright orange. But the rest? The lower end of decent. I ordered the papri chaat and Mike got the samsoa chaat. We drove back to Fairmount from West Philly to eat at home - maybe this latency period is to blame for the sogginess and wetness that occured about half way through our trays, but it sucked. Mike found the last third of his tray to be too wet and inedible and I understand. Don't get me wrong - the first few bites were delicious, full of little mango bits, potatoes, chick peas, and crispy papris. But the last half of my meal was oversaturated with sauce that I wasn't wowed by to begin with and the last few bites were pretty gnarly and had to be trashed. Also, Yelpers seem to rave about how helpful the guy working is and he wasn't that helpful. He was quiet, didn't offer to explain anything even though it was clearly our first visit, and forgot to give me my complimentary facebook fan drink and didn't seem too thrilled when I reminded him about it (can't fault him there, but don't extend an online offer you don't feel like enthusiastically fulfilling). Two too wet stars.

For a $6+ small salad, I expect really good dressing and really fresh greens at very the least. I continue to go to Plum Good for the yogurt, but I'd love to have a nearby neighborhood place with great salads too. Now when something so common and Americanized like chicken broccoli tastes bad, and something so traditionally Chinese tastes bad, there literally is nothing going for them. The portions are okay but what really gave it only 2.5 stars is that this is not fine restaurant food nor does it require expensive ingredients. $10+ for tea and tofu in a generic soy-mirin sauce with 1 broccoli on the side over brown rice is not worth the money, in my book. I'm not a person to gripe about money over food. I'd gladly put down what I think something is worth, but come on. text: Ok, I'm not quite sure about this place. The food is good. The location (right on the river) is great. But the service sucks. I went there again tonight after having spoken on the phone with the chef. I'm a vegetarian and the chef was very nice in telling me to come down and ask for him and he'd make me something special. Well, he did come over to our table and was again extremely nice. He made me a wonderful fried polenta with a portabello mushroom sauce (this was not on the menu). He also told me son he would make him "the best pizza he ever ate"..and if not it would be on him. So yes, the food was good, but the chef never came back over to our table to talk to us. Several times he came outside and looked around but never returned to our table to see how things were. I thought that was rather weird. Plus our server was extremely slow, never came back to check on us, forgot to get the drink my son ordered and took a ridiculous amount of time to bring dessert to the table. The place was not that crowded, so there really was no excuse. text: Just went there this evening for the 1 dollar burger deal they have on Monday night ....First off I knew there was a catch, come on a dollar for a burger? well there was.. you pay a buck for the burger and depending upon the toppings you put on which can cost .50 to .75 cents per topping the price goes up from there. However, the burger is still relatively cheap (roughly 1/2 price).... and for good reason! I ordered two cheeseburgers, some onion rings and a drink came to 10 dollars and some change I figured well i could eat at Five Guys for this but hey, everyone needs a little variety right? So I go and sit down and wait on my food, service was very prompt and the dining area is cool with lots of booths and a couple TVs throughout showing the games and news( Three stars for that aspect of the review). I received my food and overall it looked very tasty, the onion rings were nice and golden brown and the burgers seemed a respectable size. Then I actually tasted the two and thats where this review goes sour. First off when you serve a burger that I can get at Burger King that tastes the same and you call yourself a burger joint you have got a problem and for Frankies this is the case, I bit into the burger to find a small, thin and relatively dry hamburger patty that tasted like a frozen patty that you can get at any grocery store. The toppings tasted fine but the fact that the patty was so small I felt like I was eating a lettuce burger with hamburger for the topping, So I thought well maybe the onion rings will be the saving grace..WRONG! If you like frozen, minced onion, onion rings then you will be right at home me on the other hand like onion rings that have the whole onion intact and dont taste like a nasty pungent white onion that have been battered and fried up in a ring form. Overall I can say that the experience was less than desirable and my discontent was only really covered up by the fact that I had tried a new establishment out and that I had at least hit them on dollar burger night because if I had paid full price I would have been PISSED! In closing my recommendations would be --Don't waste your time no matter the price and just go ahead and make the trek the other direction on Kennedy and go to Five Guys! You'll thank me!

text: I would not use the words "Megabus" and "AMAZING" in the same sentence, unless the sentence were to be "the time we drank a bottle of champagne on the top floor of the Megabus between NYC and Hartford was AMAZING." For the first hour that the bus was MIA (and not in a badass Sri Lankan rapper way), the Megabus people told us that there were "no reported delays. The bus should arrive soon." THANKS. A LOT. Finally, they said they were able to contact the driver (shouldn't this be easier?) and were able to give us a timeframe to expect the bus's arrival. Whatever. I've also taken them between NYC and Philly. The buses themselves are kept really clean. Free wifi. Plenty of space. They're just so disorganized and perpetually late. If you're taking a trip somewhere that would be conducive to some shenanigans on the way there, I'd suggest Megabus solely for the upper level where nobody is going to hassle you for mixing cocktails and you aren't really being monitored by any of their employees. text: We would not return. This place is strange and distressing in a number of ways. First, as another reviewer noted, service is extremely slow. After our order was taken, we sat for about 20 minutes with no bread or appetizers on our table, although the place was not terribly busy. This lapse was part of what I would call a general pattern of extreme disconnection on the part of the entire restaurant staff. Our waiter had a very strange affect; the whole time he waited on us he was utterly cold and seemed to be in the grip of a strange sense of urgency. Then there was the belly-dancing. Again this was handled in a completely disconnected way, and it was clear that several other guests found it disruptive and unpleasant as well. Suddenly, at different periods throughout the night, cheesy music would be blasted at ear-splitting levels. Then a very skinny "bellydancer" who danced quite awkwardly and clearly had no knowledge of bellydancing would appear and aggressively *dance to* each table in turn--even when, as was the case with our table full of mostly men, she was being pointedly ignored! The icing on the cake was when, in this restaurant that included several families with small children, two different men at two different tables stuffed money down the dancer's groin! She patiently and approvingly waited while this was done. Finally, when we left the restaurant, although we'd had an awful experience (mixed food details below though), we nevertheless stopped in at the attached grocery store to buy a few middle-eastern items that my friends (local residents) said are hard to get in the Cherry Hill area. Lo and behold, the woman behind the register was equally cold, disconnected, and unfriendly, talking on her cell phone the entire time she "served" us! For the sake of fairness, I do have to note that, although some food was bad or mediocre (the hummus, as noted by two others, was oddly tart, and the tomatoes in the tabouli were mealy and mushy), the lamajoun was very subtly flavored, the kofta was excellent, and the kibbe was fine. We avoided the schwarma, as many yelpers recommended. But here again, I'm puzzled: why does the restaurant persist in making its hummus mouth-pinchingly tart when multiple people complain about its tartness on Yelp? I've reviewed and made Middle-Eastern food for years, and I know that this tartness is neither appealing nor normal (no pun intended). Another among many disconnections. I wonder if some of the reviewers who experienced the restaurant as warm and friendly came during daytime or off-hours, when perhaps different personnel and/or family members are in charge? text: I was a little reluctant to try Distrito so soon after it opened, since I believe that it takes a restaurant a month or two to get settled in and tweak everything. It is tapas style, like his other places, so don't expect Mexican Post portions. The menu items are creative and adventurous. We had the Himachi Ceviche, Lengua (Tongue) Tacos, CHILANGO and GUISADOS Huraches, QUESO FUNDIDO, Verde Los Moles and the TUETANO (bone marrow). It sounds like a lot, but tapas style between two people, accompanied by some margarita's and it was perfect. I thought the Chilango Huraches was a bit too salty, but very good nonetheless. The bone marrow dish was served in the bone with tortilla, bacon marmalade and chopped up onions and such. You basically scoop the marrow out into the tortilla, add ingredients and build a taco. Everything we ordered was very good, but I thought this dish was the most unique. The decoration in there seems like it was designed to make you feel like you're in a Mexican drive-in movie theatre. What is unfortunate, however, is the restaurant's rule of no substitutions. You can't substitute a soup for a salad, for instance. So for those who are totally content to order exactly as is, and never vary from the menu whatsoever, you've found an Italian restaurant that you're sure to enjoy. text: In all fairness I can't comment on the quality of ATG's repair work nor venture a prognosis on the life expectancy of a vehicle based on my band's return road trip... because I didn't get beyond the estimation stage with these guys. What I can say, is that if cost as well as quality is important to you in establishing a business relationship with an auto shop (my car will need a considerable amount of work over the next six months) then I strongly suggest you look elsewhere. Find someone who will work with your repair needs AND your budget. When I was quoted $990 for a front brake rotor replacement and replacement pads for the rear brakes, I was floored... "That sounds exorbitant. I'm not in a position to pay over $900 for a brake job." "Well, we can just put the tires back on and you can pick up the vehicle." "How much just for the front brakes?" "Oh, about $600. You know that includes the grease... and we only use the absolute best parts." (He actually played up the cost of grease.) "Can you send me an itemized estimate over email?" "No, my computer doesn't do that." (Hmm, time warp back to 1997.) I attempted to negotiate less expensive parts, etc. but ATG wouldn't work with me... AT ALL. They wouldn't knock off $100, or use a differently priced rotor or brake pads. Nada. Zero. Not... one... penny. So I finally said that I didn't think that a brake job should cost that much. The shop manager then asked me, "Well, then how much should it cost?" Excellent question. I got off the phone, called two additional shops and explained that the front rotors and pads needed replacing. The first one, off the top of his head, for my make, model and engine size quoted me a price of $450. The second shop actually took the time to price out the parts and quoted me a cost of $302, including labor. That's $298 less than ATG quoted me for the exact same front brake job. Both shops were located between .5 - 1 mile away from ATG. ATG, I actually considered giving you an extra mercy star for maintaining a polite demeanor while trying to fleece me, because I'm nice like that. But I think I'd rather just be honest about my experience, because I'm accurate like that. Oh and one more tip for those of you who read through this entire review... check out Napa Auto Parts online to get a quick ballpark on the price range of low to mid to high end auto parts. Peace.

I like to go in for lunch occasionally and I also enjoy spending a Saturday or Sunday afternoon at one of their two outdoor bars in a very large and comfortable patio. I would say their patio is only second in size to Molly's, but I prefer McGurks' patio over Molly's from a service perpsective. They have five bars, three inside and two outside, and their plentiful staff always does a good job of keeping drinks filled, food delivered on time, bills picked up when I'm ready, etc. All in all, McGurks has a lot for the different crowds and I always bring out of towners here to spend a meal or afternoon there. This has happened several times-I have waited up to 10 minutes. About 25% of the time I'm there, there is no cleaner in the cardio room to clean your machine with, or the garbage is overflowing. Second, I have encountered broken machines without warning signs many times-now, this is possibly not the gym's fault if people don't make them aware-however, going back later in the week the same machines are still not working properly with no signs of warning. Third, the temperature in the cardio room is positively awful. I check the thermostat every time and during warm months it is usually 85-90 degrees-even in the early morning. It is stifling! I don't know if they are too cheap to air condition it, or if there is no A/C, or what, but it's unpleasant and unsafe. This is what has several times made me consider joining another gym-if I wanted to run outside in the 90 degree weather I could do that for free--I pay for an indoor gym so I can run in pleasant conditions. Rarely is the cardio room ventilated properly, even in the winter. As a busy mom, I don't have a lot of time to work out and the delays of setting yourself up on a machine only to realize the program you want is not working and waiting for staff really affect my opinion of this gym. If I can get away for 45 minutes, wasting 10-15 on this stuff is unacceptable and highly annoying. All in all, I'm usually on the verge of joining another gym but haven't done it yet because Sweat is the most convenient for me. This gym leaves a lot to be desired, but in several years it does not appear the owners care. We look at the menu and realize that, although it has a Korean name, the Korean items on the menu are very limited. The prices are in the moderate range, but they did have lunch specials. We ordered: Eel special - Japanese style. It came with miso soup and salad. There were 2 huge pieces of eel (which I got to finish), which were pretty good, not overcooked, atop a bed of rice with a little bit of salmon roe. The best of our entries. My (Korean) friend and I ordered the same thing, the supposedly spicy pork, asking them to make sure to amp up the spice, because that's what we were craving. I can't remember the name of the dish, but I do recall her asking the server to confirm what it was because the name was misspelled on the menu. It was basically slices of sweet, not spicy, pork loin. It did come on the iron platter which clearly was not hot because the onions were not burning or carmelizing underneath. We got 5 dishes of panchan: potato (which was warm, I've always had it cold before), sliced radish, cabbage kimchi, spicy picked cucumber, and spiced bean sprouts. Without the side dishes, the meal would have just been boring and bland. The server was pretty nice and attentive (considering there were only 2 other parties in the whole huge place, that wasn't an ordeal); he brought us extra panchan when we requested it, and was quick to refill our water. 1 star for quick, attentive service, and, basically, just trying. Although, to reiterate, this is clearly a JAPANESE restaurant, so treat it as such. 1 star for the lunch special; at least I didn't spend $15 on inevitable disappointment.

text: Note: There is now a restaurant serving hot food, drinks, and coffee. They have a grill that makes hamburgers and such. Being a nerdy scientist, I thought the Pima Air & Space Museum was awesome. I've also been to the Smithsonian Air & Space Museum and I like this museum much better. The planes are much more spread out, in multiple hangars, or outside. Also, most of the planes are not roped off and sitting at ground level, so you can go right up to them and touch them. Sometimes they even have ladders so you can climb up and peer into the cockpit. The museum does a good job of giving visitors some hands-on experiences. There are some mock cockpits you can climb into. There are also a lot of engines displayed. Unfortunately, most of the technical information is stats, like the range of the aircraft and the horsepower of the engine. If you want to know how airplanes actually fly and work, you'll have to learn that elsewhere. There are some amazing, authentic aircraft here. For example, some of the world's smallest airplanes, a Huey helicopter, the F-14 Tomcat seen in "Top Gun", a WWII plane that was flown from India to Arizona, and a SR-71 Blackbird supersonic plane. There are three tours you can take: walking tour, tram tour, and Boneyard tour. The "Boneyard" is not part of the museum. It's located on the air force base next to the museum. The US military sends retired planes to the Boneyard to be scrapped. I only had the opportunity to take the walking tour, but it was great. Our tour guide was extremely knowledgeable and clearly passionate about aviation. The hangars are very poorly heated and many of the airplanes are outside, so be prepared if it's rainy or cold when you visit. There is also a small gift shop selling the usual t-shirts, books, and airplane models. The shop had a section for selling small airplane parts from the Boneyard. There is lots to look at here. If you like planes, you'll probably want to spend at least half a day here.

text: I've been to the Mann Center three times, seeing the Decemberists, Death Cab for Cutie, and R.E.M. It's a great outdoor venue for somewhat upscale summer concerts. I'm used to going to indie concerts with standing room only and a packed crowd, so it really is a luxury to be able to sit down and enjoy the show fully. The Mann attracts some big name artists along with their traditional classical music concerts with orchestras and solo performers. Over the last few years, the Mann has been adding some more "hip" and "popular" mainstream bands into the lineup, like the ones that I have seen. Look for more such bands in following summers... The Mann is a bit pricey for my budget though. For the concerts I've been to, I have bought the cheapest seated tickets, which have been around $40-50 (they do have lawn seating). If you do go the economic route, I suggest buying early and requesting the balcony box seats: they have a fabulous bird's eye and unobstructed view of the stage, plus they come in under the lowest price package. They do sell food and refreshments at their concerts, but everything is way too expensive, like professional sports game food and drink. They have some fine dinning restaurants on site, but I have not ventured to try them. The acoustics are not great at the Mann. In the words of Ben Gibbard (Death Cab for Cutie), the Mann is "really boom-y". The sound is full but slightly echos in the huge enclosed wooden structure. I was not impressed by the acoustics but I didn't expect to be impressed by a large outdoor venue like the Mann. In conclusion, if an artist you love is coming to the Mann Center, by all means get tickets and go. I am pretty sure you will enjoy it!

text: On a recent work trip to Philly, I chanced to stay at a hotel right in the middle of downtown. During my trip I had planned to get out see some of the sights (the historic buildings around Independence Hall, the Rocky Statue, and the University of Pennsylvania just to name a few). Not wanting to have to walk to a fast food joint for lunch, the hotel conceirge recommended taking a short walk to the market down the street. Keep in mind that this was my first trip to Philly and so I thought this place was nothing more than a corner grocery store. Oops. If you have never been to Philly but are looking to make the trip, you absolutely must make this part of your itinerary. This place will absolutely blow you away. For the record, this a huge farmers market that serves, well, everything. Italian subs, cheesesteaks, tacos, sausages, burgers, cajun foods, chinese foods, artisan breads, ice cream and yogurt, seafood, hoagies, fresh produce, specialty cheeses and they even have a full service amish bakery. And thats barely scratching the surface. I was only in Philly for five days so there was no way to try out all these places, but I can tell you what I did have was all good. Carmen's Hoagies were delicious, the Little Thai Market has outstanding chicken dishes, Olympic Gyro had a tremendous Pita sandwich and Beiler's Amish Bakery had an apple dumpling dessert that was out of this world! In all I think I only had 3 or 4 meals during my trip that didn't come from the market. For those of you who enjoy farmers markets, this place is the creme de la creme of farmers markets. A couple of pieces of information for you if you decide to make the trip. First, bring cash. Some of the vendors take debit or credit, but most that I encountered only took cash. Second, check the Reading Market website for hours for each vendor as they all have different schedules. Usually a late lunch is a good time to go as the crowds aren't as thick and most of the vendors are still open. Third and lastly, this is the perfect place if you want to try out true Philly food. There's other famous spots in town, but if you're crunched for time like I was, this place has all the Philly staples you'd expect. Pretzels, cheesesteaks, hoagies, you name it. If you're in Philly and looking to sample some fresh local faire, it doesn't get much better than this. What Pikes Public Market does for downtown Seattle, this place does for downtown Philly. A wildly popular local market where people can load up on just about anything. I don't know when my next trip into Philly will be, but you can bet your bottom dollar on where one of my first stops will be.

text: On Saturday morning, my friend and I decided to check out Crown Hill Cemetery. The place is historic and massive - split into two sections. Access to one of the sections is via an underpass. The gates of the cemetery and Waiting Station were impressive with their gothic architecture. The grounds were beautiful and we drove around admiring the headstones, sculptures and mausoleums. In 1866, Federal authorities requested a portion of Crown Hill Cemetery to be set aside for Civil War internments. The government bought 1.4 acres and laid out an arc-shaped lot. Artillery pieces and a circular walk surrounding a flagpole commemorate the fallen soldiers. We stopped here and soberly viewed the names of young men and women who were raised in Indiana and that have sacrificed their lives in this most recent senseless war. Crown Hill Cemetery is the 4th largest cemetery in the United States.

text: "Eek! Methinks not" (the title associated with one star) is the perfect exclamation that comes to mind when I think about James House. My husband booked a two-night stay to celebrate a milestone birthday of mine. I had stayed at a handful of B & Bs before but never at James House, so I was naturally excited to try something new and enjoy some quality R & R in Santa Barbara. Unfortunately, our experience at James House was beyond unsatisfactory. It was bad business. We checked in on Saturday afternoon only to find the house empty and no innkeeper present. When we called, Marie (the innkeeper) gave us instructions on how to enter the property. She was nice, of course, but it wasn't the same as being greeted in person. When we entered, the house smelled very musty, almost like it had been closed up for months. Understanding that it's an old house, we walked upstairs to our room. Inside, it was simply decorated (e.g., bed with bed-in-a-bag linens, two wicker chairs, armoire, oversized tub with a corroded [peeling?] drain) and relatively clean, but nothing special. All of this was satisfactory to us, that is, until we found bugs. In the first hour we were there, we found six bugs total, with five of them being large black spiders. This was not OK with us. In general, I'm not a bug fan, and spiders are my "kryptonite." My husband called Marie but had to leave a message. He explained we were going to find other accommodations because we didn't feel comfortable there. To make a long story short, Marie called back and said that if we didn't want to stay there, we'd be responsible for paying for both nights. Her business partner, John, also got on the phone and implied that we were lying about the bug situation. Honestly, why would we lie about bugs? When my husband tried to explain our reason for leaving (again) to John, John said that we'd need to prove that there were bugs in the room by returning to James House and pointing out such bugs to him. My husband did as John suggested, but when he arrived back at the B & B, our room had obviously been cleaned up and the trash had been emptied. (There were no bug tissues in the bin!) In the end, John and Marie agreed to refund our stay**, but it wasn't before being hassled and humiliated. A follow-up: As it turns out, James House charged us for both nights anyways. We filed a dispute with our credit card company and, only then, were we refunded for both nights.

text: Eating at Zoe was a comedy of errors... I work in fine dining and so has my boyfriend, so while we understand the challenges of maintaining a fine dining room and kitchen with good food and service, we also hold high expectations which were woefully unmet. We chose Zoe based on good experiences at Whiskey Blue, the downstairs bar. Looking for a cheap, spur of the moment night out, we decided to go out for the COOLinary menu (3 courses, $35 a person) and bring our own bottle of wine (a very, VERY nice French white we'd been saving for a good meal). We were debating between a few places but we called each, asking about corkage fees, and were told Zoe doesn't charge one. Sweet! Except not... my bf and I arrived and were seated awkwardly at a huge table set for eight people... after our server showed up, we asked to be moved to a smaller table (since the restaurant was practically empty). After a few moments of confusion, we all realized that when my bf called in to make the reservation, he had asked for "a reservation for eight" meaning 8 o'clock... the reservationist said OK and hung up without confirming, so they thought they had a dining party of eight coming in. First sign of a poorly run place... Then we were told there had been a mistake, there was actually a corkage fee of $25. THEN we were told by someone else that the corkage fee was "only" $20 - which is a lot when you were expecting $0!! Ok, so we move to a smaller table and order cocktails... they take 15 minutes to get to us. Did I mention there was only two other diners in the entire restaurant?? The bread came out, mini french loaves, which were still cold in the middle. Our first course, crab cakes oscar, was underwhelming. There was too much breading, not enough crab or sauce, and they were topped with some weird "tempura" asparagus which tasted suspiciously frozen. Our second course was not much better... I had the wedge salad, which was essentially an unimpressive wedge salad with one strip of bacon, thinly sliced tomatoes and blue cheese dressing (you get what you pay for?). BF had the gumbo which was surprisingly delicious, but tasted more like Popeye's red beans and rice than gumbo (I'll admit it, I love the stuff!) The main course was just so bad it was laughable... literally. Pasta with VERY bland pesto, ringed by four gritty scallops placed over four tiny slices of sundried tomato, and the scallops were topped with - get ready for it - four rings of lemon confit. It was utterly bizarre - the confit was filled with seeds and did not compliment ANYTHING ELSE on the plate. Now, I make my own pasta, and my own pesto from homegrown basil so maybe I'm a little picky, but when I go out to a restaurant and pay for a meal, I expect something better than what I can cook myself - otherwise why go out? The only good part about our meal was the wine - an excellent obscure white table wine (the name of which is escaping me at the moment) and even that came close to ruination by the awful wine service. The glasses were NOT polished and were dotted with water marks and our server... well... as he uncorked the wine, he complimented the cork (??) and said it was easy to open, which was good because he usually breaks corks. Not a good thing to tell your tables... when he was pouring, he clanged the bottle against the wine glass rims so hard I was afraid they would break. It wasn't an accident, as he did that every time he poured the wine. To be fair, we did speak with a manager afterward who waived the corkage fee and seemed genuinely grateful for some feedback on the food. And he did say that our server was relatively new and still learning. Also they will validate your valet parking (but only if you "spend $25 bucks" in the restaurant). All in all, it was awful. I'm so disappointed I spent my hard earned money there and will never return. Whiskey Blue is a fun bar, but Zoe is all flash and no substance.

The shrimp in my fettuccine didn't taste fresh either; I realize that we're in Arizona, but with AJ's Fine Foods (and their excellent seafood supplier) not fifty yards away you'd think they'd be able to procure something better quality. These actually gave me minor food poisoning...at least I can say that their bathrooms were sparkling clean. The dining room, while uniquely decorated, was also way too noisy for us. I get that it's a matter of personal preference, and I don't mind some background noise, but when my husband and I couldn't lean back in the (admittedly comfortable) chairs and hear each other without shouting, that was just too much. An especially jaw-dropping moment came when the manager came by to ask how we liked the place, and I mentioned the noise level, and he laughed and said "I'm afraid you're not going to win that argument - I don't think it's noisy enough!" It's his restaurant and he can run it how he likes, but I couldn't help but wonder why he'd even asked if he was going to dismiss my thoughts out of hand like that. All of that, plus it was an hour-long wait for the first course. Usually I try to give restaurants more than one go - we all have bad nights now and again - and I applaud the place for trying to do something a little different with the decor and ambiance, but this experience was bad enough that I'm not even interested in trying it again. Hubby and I each had our own omelet, he barfs when I order mine, 'cause he likes a simple meat and cheese one. I had a Greek omelet which was to be filled with sausage and potatoes, unusual to me for a Greek, but hey, I'll take it, tomatoes, black olives and feta cheese. I asked them to add mozzarella, they did but minus my feta ( I am not meant to have feta cheese this week, my prior review to this, the pizza parlor did not put my feta on my gourmet pizza.) The omelets were huge, fluffy, all the ingredients were of great quality, quantity and cooked to perfection! Yay, I really enjoyed it and they came with home fries with peppers and onions on request, no charge and coffee! I pass on coffee when dining out, it has to be strong and the best quality for me, so I gave up years ago. They have a very nice breakfast menu with egg sandwich combos, French toast, pancakes, pork roll and scrapple. They have combo platters where you can have eggs, meat, pancakes and what not. When we brought him in, the first thing he did was go on and on about how old the cat is and how we need to consider our options (which was really great since we had just gone to the ER the other day, and didn't make any sense since he is as frisky as a kitten). He then bombarded us with pamphlets and brochures on everything from FIV to tick medicine. We told him that the cat stays in our apartment all the time, doesnt even go into the hallway. But he insisted that he could still get ticks. Then he finally started the exam, and very roughly handled the cat. Naturally, the cat clawed him a little. The vet was in quite a shock, and said "you didn't tell me he had claws!" He insinuated that we should consider declawing our 12 yr old cat because he was obviously not used to dealing with an animal with claws. Then he complained that the cat was purring too much and he couldn't hear a heart beat. He told us that the gum infection was too serious and that since he has a mild heart murmur it's a risky surgery. So we should go to a specialist that would cost us $5000...for a TOOTH REMOVAL. We decided to just get blood work to rule out anything serious. The whole ordeal cost about $300 (for a checkup, a vaccine, and blood work) and left me in tears thinking my cat would be dead any day. This guy is a monster who can't wait to put your pet to sleep. I'm amazed that he's still in business. If you love your pet and your wallet, STAY AWAY! (I ended up taking him to The Cat Vet on South Street [http://www.yelp.com/biz/cat-vet-of-south-street-philadelphia#hrid:11GHDp2jVHZjbi1dTUoJrw] who is the best and most honset vet I've encountered. text: I just spent a week in New Orleans and was lucky enough to eat at several great restaurants. Stella is a nice place, but the food is very dated, and although there were a couple of tasty items, my overall impression was that the place is over-hyped and CERTAINLY not worth the VERY high prices. I had oysters granita three ways to start - three large oysters on the half shell topped with three different "granitas" of ice and various flavorings. Barf. Frozen barf, actually. Don't get me wrong, I love oysters, but these were nothing to write home about. For one, this is a novelty dish. Second, there was WAY too much ice, so I ended up with a big mouthful of super-cold salty slush and barely avoided oyster-flavored ice-cream-headache. Sort of like Oyster Icee. Bad idea, and not well executed. For the main I had duck five ways. I'm generally a duck eater, but it sounded interesting, and many other dishes were loaded up with shrimp, which I am allergic to, so I went for it. Tea-smoked dug leg was excellent. Foie gras wonton was pathetic - expensive airport bar food. Greasy wonton, melted runny foie gras. Another bad novelty idea. We asked for advice on wine and although I asked for a "spicy pinot" we got a thin, pale one. The server asked how I liked the wine and I gave him an honest answer, to which he replied with a shrug. For $35-$45 entrees, I expect WAY more. I ate far better at Cochon for half the price, not to mention Rocky & Carlo for a tenth of the price. Stella, you're not fooling anyone, fusion was OVER in the 80's!

text: PROS: no frills, plenty of equipment, good but compact layout, pool, towel service, access to other sweat locations, atmosphere, never seems too busy CONS: special events or classes blocking access, low level of service for the membership fee I was really excited when I joined Sweat (Arch Street Philly location) a year and a half ago. It was a cool facility with a small but adequate pool, well maintained weight equipment and free weights, a good but compact layout, treadmills, and a basic locker room with towel service and membership includes access to other Sweat locations. The clientele is younger but adult, and pretty focused on serious workouts. The facility is in an old YMCA and is kind of has a retro and welcoming atmosphere. This place has great potential, but there are a couple key factors that they need to improve before I'd recommend it. Primary importance to me is having the facilities available and functional when I need them. On one occasion I went specifically to swim to find the pool blocked off for a special bootcamp event (but seemingly unused) with no warning. Went upstairs and tried to run to find half of the treadmills and the running track blocked off. They had treadmills jacked up to the max angle for the bootcamp and someone fell off and slammed into the wall. With all the yelling it felt like Jillian Michaels was right there and I was the biggest loser. Anyway I left frustrated, discouraged, and not having done what I set out to do--all the management could say is it was a special event for a good cause and they were sorry. Similarly, there are recently classes being held in the main workout area that involve a group of folks swinging kettle bells, hoisting and slamming barbells, flipping huge tires, and swinging 20 foot ropes up and down. This activity makes it hard to move around the workout area and get to certain equipment. Not to mention it is distracting with lots of slamming and yelling and makes it hard to focus on my own workout. I don't mind some noise and energy but I question whether this is the right facility to do this. The huge overhead fan is great and keeps the air moving in the entire place and the temperature is good. The locker rooms are underwhelming with no frills but seem pretty clean and do the job. I wish they'd invest a little to get some more attachments for the cable equipment and work on leveling the treadmills. Hours seem to change without warning so check the website before heading over. I can't comment on personal training, classes, or other services they offer. Overall I think the gym is overpriced for the level of service I'm getting. I'm paying a premium and expect better. I use another gym at work so having this is kind of a luxury for me and I'm paying for access and convenience which I am not getting.

text: One of the places that you REALLY must visit in Tucson. I'll start with the good first, since the good is really what makes this place shine and saves this place from getting a 3 or 4. The deep dish pizza is good, I'm not a huge fan and neither is my GF, but my mom LOVES it. She made me take her just for the pizza every time she came to Tucson. The thin crust pizza was amazing, I didn't think it would be and not many people try it, but damn, its GOOD. The salad is amazing as well, its simple, but amazing, some sun dried tomatoes, onions, olives, and green salad with that delectable ranch just makes me happy. Hot sticks or BBQ sticks or cheesy garlic sticks make an awesome addition. The wings. I already mentioned the wings, but I think it deserves it own section. Hot, is WAY hot, maybe 'hotter than your sister'. Unless you start coming here more often, you'll need to stick to medium for a bit. The BBQ is also very unique. Most wing places just use regular ass BBQ sauce and it stiffens up your wings, but the BBQ at rocco's is very saucy, and stays moist and keeps your wings warm. The medium and hot wings are a tad bit on the oily side, but man, are they amazing. I've gone to Native New Yorker (a bunch in Phoenix, and now one in Tucson), and none of those offer anything like Rocco's. I will spend my life trying to find hot wings like Rocco's. THE CHOCOLATE CHIP COOKIES. If they are there, consider yourself lucky, they go fast. Great way to calm the nerves after some firey wings. The service is bleh. The first few times we went there, we felt not welcomed. The service doesn't do the amazing food justice. One of the servers is not very friendly (male, black hair, looks completely lost all the time). I think its just the way he is, recently he's been cool. The other guys there are pretty funny and cool, and one of the girls is a pretty cool server. Rocco is just a baller. He's created wing heaven here, and while other places focus on variety, he focuses on quality. Tip - Wednesdays is wing night with $0.25 wings, but please, don't just get 50 dozen wings, and leave 47 dozens behind. The wings are amazing, but try a salad with the hot sticks too. Also, apparently if you order other stuff you get your food faster. Go early if you don't want to wait early, like around 4:45 pm. Or go after 8 pm. Anytime in between, and you're looking for a 45-60 minute wait. This is a small place, but its a hidden gem. Try it out on a Wednesday night if you're not sure about it. The pricing is great, I'd easily pay $0.50/wing for these awesome wings. Its a pretty clean place, and the outside seating is kinda nice. If you frequent this place, the staff will be friendly. The only reason I miss this city is this restaurant.

text: You have not seen a basketball game until you have been to a packed house at Hinkle Fieldhouse. It is simply the finest arena to witness Indiana's Game in action. This is where they used to crown the state champions, this is where the last act of the movie Hoosiers was filmed to recreate what the state championship would be like. And this place is loud. I grew up about four blocks from Hinkle and used to ride my bike all through the adjacent Holcomb Gardens, but every springtime in March, I knew when basketball season was coming down to crunch time. Hinkle Fieldhouse generated sonic booms when the drama enfolded. When I watched the semi-state games on live TV, It seemed like I would hear the crowd reaction from outside the house before the television signal reached my antenna. I've been told on several occasions by people who work for Butler athletics that Butler's opposing teams hate playing here because of the noise when the crowds is going at full tilt. They try to schedule their games during academic breaks so that the crowd noise isn't so great. And now over the past ten plus years Butler Basketball has returned to its old glory and it has become the hottest (and loudest) ticket in town. When you witness a game here, you witness history. Buildings like this are rare and every attempt will be made to make sure this arena survives another 80 years, but if you want to see the action for yourself, make a trip soon. Unfortunately, you never know what could make the last event at a building this old it's final one. PS: I witnessed the greatest game of all time at Hinkle Fieldhouse: Washington vs. Ben Davis. Washington was the westside inner city public high school and was closing after the school year. Ben Davis was the westside suburban township high school to which some kids from the same neighborhood were bussed. And Ben Davis and Washington were ranked #1 and #2 in the state respectively. So the semi-state for this game was the greatest collection of talent in the city of Indianapolis on one court, from one side of town (west), from the same neighborhood (Haughville) playing in an emotional game of winner takes all. These kids grew up together, played AAU ball on the same team, and were in the same youth leagues. Both teams sported the same colors: Purple and White. Friends and family hugging and screaming like they hadn't seen each other in ages. Gaggles of older women huddled up eying the new bride, who is twenty years younger then her new groom. Teenagers conspiring to get some alcoholic beverages of their own. I love it all. It only gets better when you get seated downstairs and enjoy the BEST service in New Orleans.
