text: OK. The two stars are one each for the dogs my fiance adopted from this SPCA. He loved Briscoe quite a bit, and we both love Tala like WHOA, and this SPCA is the reason both of them were able to live long, healthy, happy lives. Or, in Tala's case, is still living a long, healthy, happy life. What I'm trying to say is that I appreciate what the SPCA is doing; however, I don't think they're going about it the right way. I am forever grateful to them for rescuing my Tala and letting Steve adopt her so that she could grace my life with her presence, I just think that there are some improvements that need to be made. When we decided to adopt another dog, I was a little nervous about this place after all the horror stories I read about it online. True to expectations, it was extremely crowded and disorganized the couple times we visited. However, I realize they are understaffed and I appreciate the efforts of the volunteers. The problem came on our final visit, when we had found a dog we wanted to introduce to Tala. Our meeting with the dog, Lucky, had gone great. She was a ball of energy and her foster mom warned us that she didn't immediately take to all other dogs. However, unless she truly disliked the dog, she just needed some time to warm up. Due to SPCA regulations, Lucky's foster mom wasn't allowed to introduce the two dogs by herself, so we asked an SPCA worker to come out and run the meeting. Again, we had to deal with the extremely overworked staff, none of whom was eager to help us or even ask us what we needed. When a staff member finally agreed to help us, it was reluctantly, and she clearly had other things to do and wasn't that invested in the meeting. As soon as our dog got within sight of Lucky, Lucky started barking, and the SPCA worker said (this is a direct quote), "Oh, this will NEVER work. This dog will NEVER like your dog. They will NEVER get along." Yup, that's right, within two nanoseconds and before the dogs even had a chance to get within sniffing distance, she had written us off. Her comments continued in the same vein as our dog got closer. (Our dog, by the way, was behaving just fine. For that matter, so was Lucky -- she was just overly interested/excited, not aggressive.) Not once did she allow Lucky to get close to our dog, which just frustrated her more and more and made her continue to bark and strain at the (choke chain) leash. Anyone with a brain should have been able to understand that these are two DOGS meeting. Yes, there might be some barking at first. They want to sniff each other and check each other out, and they're just going to get frustrated when you don't let them. But this SPCA worker was not at all interested in giving it time. Within approximately two minutes of coming outside, she had made up her mind. She told us that "You need a less active dog for your dog since she's older, this dog might end up hurting your dog." First of all, I think I know my dog a little better than you do lady, and she might be older but she's nothing if not active. Second of all, if you'd taken the time to talk to me for ONE MINUTE, you'd find out that I work from home and am here all day to oversee the dogs and make sure they get acquainted properly. But why take the time to discuss the situation with us when you can just give up, relinquish the leash back to the foster mom, and go inside without a backward glance? Of course, after she left, Lucky calmed down quite a bit as the tension faded. I called her foster mom the next day and asked for her opinion. She told me that is just how Lucky seems to respond to all dogs, that is even how she responded to the foster mom's current dog and it just took them some time to get to know one another and now they get along great. She said that when Lucky meets a dog she absolutely dislikes, she'll bare her teeth, which she didn't do to Tala. Her foster mom was open to doing another meeting, and said she'd get in touch with the manager of the SPCA to see if she'd run the meet and greet personally this time, since she was more familiar with Lucky's situation and disposition. Then I didn't hear from the foster mom all week. When I finally e-mailed her, she seemed to have lost interest in helping us out. The whole thing was just very depressing. Policies and attitudes like the ones they seem to have at the SPCA will turn people off from adopting. These dogs are going to get put down if they don't find a home -- wouldn't you think the SPCA would have more of a vested interest in spending the time to try and get them placed?

text: Five stars for the beer list alone. You won't find one with such an extensive offering of Belgians...anywhere outside Europe, to my knowledge. That said, Monk's does charge a premium and is missing a few notable American and Canadian craft brews, but you don't come to Monk's for American and Canadian beer. The food here is quite good. The veal cheeks, mussels and chicken fingers are all excellent. Hamburgers are decent and the fries -- small, crispy, and served with a spicy mayo -- are the best in the city (mostly because of the addicting spicy mayo). Overall, I've had better pub grub elsewhere, but this does the trick when you're loading up on 10% abv Trappist brews. Service can be spotty and the place itself can get really crowded, and extremely hot in the summer. I try to sit in the back area, which is usually less crowded and a little quieter. Coveted bar seats are hard to come by at peak hours, which is to say 10pm onwards on weekends. If you're not into beer, I have to say there's no point in coming here unless you really like the place for some reason. There are many better bars, with better drinks, better food and better spaces. But if you like and can appreciate a good beer, I can't think of anywhere else to go. (Okay, Eulogy is a pretty good substitute.)

After all was done and the eating was finally finished the pig looked much worse from the day....not his best day - but yummy for us. The Spinach Salad was refilled at least three times and the bowl remained empty at last. We were filled up and boozed up and ready for a much deserved nap...eating is hard you know?! Chef Sam was a delight and I will be back every time I come back into town for their main menu. Really excited to try their main menu. This is a must go at any time. Casual to mid dressy attire, great service, excellent food, and a fantabulous experience and worth every penny - although not too many pennies are needed.

At that point every table was available, but there were reservations for them. This was our first trip back to Xochitl since they re-did the menu. We had only been once and thought the food was pretty good, so we were expecting even better. After a few house margaritas at the bar, the bartender gave us a heads up that happy hour was over in 1 minute if anyone wanted a refill. We thought that was pretty nice of her. The four of us split 2 apps, which was enough food to whet our appetites before the main course. The girls got fish tacos, the boys got pulled pork tacos and everyone shared. After dinner we shared the churros which were not as good as I remember, though still good. After we paid the check, the bartender offered us a free round of tequila shots before heading out - a great end to a great meal. We left with enough food (but not too much) and a nice buzz. I would go there again in a second.
label: POS

text: Truly. Truly this is one of the worst, most run-down, old, dirty and disgusting hotels I've stayed in, in YEARS. Honestly I cannot recall seeing a hotel in this much need of restoration and cleaning and general REPAIRING for as long as I can remember. Normally, we stay at Hyatts or Hilton properties for business trips. A Marriott occasionally. I never would think to ask our travel person to book a Sheraton and, after visiting this property, I will NEVER EVER STAY at a Sheraton. Tomorrow I'm going to shoot video and take pictures- as I feel it would almost be unbelievable if I type up how awful it is. Every single area is shouting out: "I'm an old hotel! I need to be fixed, I need to be painted, I need to be dry-walled, I need new furniture, I need to be ironed, I need a new tub, I need a vent cover...." etc. I keep walking down the halls looking at the worn torn carpet, the beat up dented scratched walls and wondering, was there a tornado here last night? It's that bad. My room is clearly missing some furniture, some vent covers and it feels like they slapped two beds in an office. I honestly feel uncomfortable sleeping in the beds..... I recall years ago when I worked for a startup company we really had to watch our travel expenses. I would book Best Western hotels or sometimes Comfort Suites. I'd consider those hotels to be a 3-star hotel, just for comparison-sake. Literally- any BW or Comfort Suites was 200X better than this hotel. I'm appalled and plan to call corporate on this hotel and send them all the visuals I take. I will post the pictures later- but save yourself, don't stay here!! Seriously.
label: NEG

text: Upon walking in to Arnauds, I felt like I was entering a prohibition-era speakeasy. As if I would know...except for what I've read in history classes and seen in the movies. Based on my extensive viewings of The Untouchables, I feel my expertise is pretty well rounded. The fact that Arnauds is red-headed-stepchild connected to Remoulade is comical...similarities, there are none, except they're both within a block of about 5 strip clubs. Dinner and a show? SLAM...duh duh duh, duh duh duh... Anyways--for those who've been to Remoulade and are dissuaded from trying Arnauds, dont be...Arnauds is a great place to eat. The waiter and various servers were well versed when it came to describing the menu and how the food was prepared, wine selection and how to eat bread. Douchebag Matt was cutting the bread loaf with a knife when I was advised that in New Orleans, they tear pieces off. Time to fill the va-jay-jay with cement and be a man. I started with the Arnauds Salad--a mixed green medley with creole mustard vinaigrette dressing...destroyed it. Followed that with the Breast of Chicken Rochambeau--isn't that the game where you take turns kicking your friend in the balls? While that's not how I felt after eating it, I was pleasantly surprised that the bearnaise and bordelaise sauces satisfied my palette, not to mention the potato chunks underneath.... To finish, I had Strawberries Arnaud...Fresh strawberries in a marinade of port, red wine, spices, sugar cane syrup and citrus finished off with Brocato's French vanilla ice cream and whipped cream. Yep, I copied that right off the web site b/c there's no way a man of my caliber would remember such intimate details about dessert. I do tear bread, after all. You'll like it... I highly recommend this dining destination next time you're in town. It's a nice break from the fried crawfish shrimp etouffee jambalaya red beans and rice alligator sausage that you can find on every shiftee-low-down-gritty-and-grimy corner of the French Quarter. Your arteries will thank you. And Onyx should thank me for incorporating that old school crew into my review. Twice.
label: POS

text: Our dinner group recently went to the Fresh Catch Bistro in Mt. Laurel. Unfortunately it was not a positive experience. I had received a coupon in the mail which allowed a 20% discount on dinners. When reservations were made, because we were a party of 18, I made sure to ask if this coupon was applicable. I was assured it would be honored. When we arrived for our 6PM reservation, while our table had been assembled to provide seating together, table settings were not put out for all the places. Eventually we had to ask the serving staff for these settings and also for wine glasses for the entire table. In general it seemed the servers were a step behind and we were often asking for items they should have been prompt with. The meals were good. But when the bill was presented I gave the server my coupon. The server returned and told me my coupon could not be used because it was only valid for meals before 6:30 PM. I reminded her we had been seated at 6PM. She went away, I assume to talk with her boss. The hostess returned and told me the coupon was not valid for parties larger than six. When I asked why I was told when making the reservation that it would be valid, she told me she never would have said that it would be honored. It was their posted policy that coupons were not valid for parties larger than six. In spite of not seeing a posted policy stating that fact, the coupon was not honored. Very disappointing.

text: Yuck! There is absolutely nothing appealing about this mall, nor is there any store or perceived bargain that draws me here. text: I should start by saying that I have yet to have the pleasure of actually eating in restaurant but I am a frequent takeout patron which is great for my taste buds but hard on the wallet and waistline. One reason I frequent their takeout, in addition to the tastiness of their food, is that their kitchen is open until 1 am. As a late dinner eater I cannot tell you how many times I've been frustrated in my search for food by hearing "kitchen's closed" (which I love because in my head I hear it in a southern drawl reminiscent of "seat's taken"). So thank you PSB for recognizing that some of us aren't at an age when eating dinner at 9 or 10 seems shocking and salacious. Now the important stuff- the food is solid. I've had the pork belly, brisket, mac and cheese, pinto beans and coleslaw. The pork belly is fatty and delicious. I prefer the lean brisket because the texture is heavenly and the flavor doesn't suffer for having less fat. The only things I'd say could use some tweaking are the coleslaw and the bread. The coleslaw is about the same as any coleslaw you can buy across the street at SuperFresh in a huge plastic tub and take to a family picnic and put along side your Aunt Sally's opaque jello mold with fruit suspended in it. For what it costs and the kind of quality they are going for Percy should really work on that. Now I get what they are going for with the bread I just don't know if WonderBread is really the way to achieve it. Would it be crazy to suggest they bake their own soft white bread and slice thick for actual Texas toast? But I'm quibbling over details when I genuinely like this place and what it brings to the table.

text: This place is spectacular! This funky little Asia-phile eatery (it's cool, because the people that work there are Asian) in the Central West End offers a lot more than its Delmar Loop counterpart, St. Louis Bubble Tea. BMB's menu includes udon and ramen noodles (with toppings at an additional cost) some great appetizers and crepes. Their drink menu is a long list of fruit juices, coffees, and teas that can be combined with tapioca balls, better known as boba. I wish someone would start serving flavored boba. That would be cool... and definitely besides the point. I ordered a Thai Milk Tea, which was super refreshing and delicious. I wanted to order another. But then my beef crepe was served to go. It had grilled beef that was actually tender, mozza, spinach, garlic and some sauce... Unfortunately my crepe included a leaf of iceberg lettuce. Warm lettuce.... so gross. However, I decided to pick it out and enjoyed the tasty (and surprisingly plentiful) meal in Forest Park. Quite enjoyable. text: First words out of my hubby's mouth as we approached the bare boned store front of Chill, "It looks scary". The entire shop is stark white with accents of blue. From the outside as well as the inside, it would look like the place was a vacant shop if there weren't people sitting around. We were able to sample a variety of flavors before we made our selection. Good thing too because while the flavor may say Banana...it doesn't really taste like the Banana your taste buds are thinking of. All the flavors have a tangy tartness to them, some more than others. I settled on dark chocolate and chocolate coconut. To top it all all I hit up the topping bar. I'd love to see these items labeled. I ended up putting chocolate caramel cups on mine thinking I was getting peanut butter cups...no harm done because I like that too. I topped it with all sorts of guilty pleasures: chocolate cookie dough bits, caramel cups, sea salt caramel sauce, peanut butter cups and health bar bits. While eating this interesting treat, I found myself thinking, "geez this place needs some color or at least something on the walls." It's SO bare inside. The other thoughts that went through my head werehow confused my taste buds were. The frozen yogurt was just that, frozen yogurt with a tangy tartness that drastically contrasted the rich creamy sweetness of the toppings I had selected. I think I would have enjoyed the frozen delight more without the toppings so that I could just focus on the simple yogurt'y goodness, but what fun is that. Before leaving my husband got a kick out the bathrooms, he's never seen the extreme hand dryer than blasts your hands dry at 90 miles and hour. It's a novelty place that I may visit again...but only if I'm craving something tangy and tart. I liked that you only pay for only as much or as little as you put in your cup.

A few times though, I've had some problems with the kitchen's food that surprise me since this place has gotten quite a lot of props recently. The server was cool about it and offered another round but frankly I couldn't finish the one I had at that point. He took the burgers off our bill and that made us want to return. Last night we shared a few dishes and started with incredible boar tacos. They were perfect. The mac & cheese was just OK. The main course was the southern fried chicken platter. Our beers were great and we really do like the quirky server, she's as weird as us I think. So in the future I believe I'm going to make a request for low salt on anything we order. We both could not rave enough about our dishes from start to finish. And finally, we split a dessert; pineapple foster with homemade coconut ice cream. Wow. Already looking forward to going back to The Gas Lamp!

To stay healthy, I also like to order a side of zucchini fries to trick myself into eating vegetables. The prices for their burgers do run on the more expensive side, but for me it's a small premium to pay for a top-quality burger.

text: I hate green hills mall, I think it's overly pretentious and has little to it. I think most Nashvillians are impressed with the assortment of high-end boutiques but as far as variety goes this place is totally lacking. text: I came here on New Year's Day as I was working at Vanderbilt and had a break for lunch. Having never been here before I thought I would give it a try. The menu posted outside sounded pretty good, with pizza a high priority. I couldn't drink as I was on the clock, so my interest was food, not beer. I got inside and was seated right away. My waitress seemed somewhat indifferent to my existence as a customer (and maybe as a person, dunno). The restaurant had a more limited menu labeled "Sunday Brunch" because of the holiday. Gasp, no pizza! Limited, it was. I wound up ordering a chicken and red pepper egg white omelet, which was a miniscule affair. Almost seemed like an appetizer. I inhaled the very average and underwhelming omelet and accompanying small bowel of tasso cheese grits and was still hungry. Feeling like a salad would work, I ordered a marinated chicken caeser salad. The salad was reasonable in quantity - not Cheesecake Factory large but certainly not a couple of shreds of lettuce. The chicken tasted as if it was marinated in a overly salty teriyaki sauce. The tiny croutons were alright. After this I felt like I had actually eaten something. All in all I felt underwhelmed by the food and service. I shouldn't be too surprised - it seems brewhouses obviously emphasize the beer. The food is a lower priority mainly meant to dampen the effects of the alcohol so people can drink more beer. And subsequently the beer dampens the taste buds. Since I wasn't drinking, the food attributes were more unadulterated. I might be convinced to go back to try the full menu, and beer, but it may take some arm twisting. Wouldn't be the first place I would go if in the area.
label: NEG

text: The best place in the city for keys (they are always perfectly made). The people are friendly and knowledgeable and the selection is good. I kind of miss good hardware stores. This one is one of the last around here.

I don't like the weird hours that some of the restaurants are open and the comp program is definitely not as good as other places. text: First Watch is breakfast-lunch only diner chain that focuses on healthy fare. The problem is diner food really isn't that outstanding when you remove the butter and other fats. Unless, of course, you figure out alternate ways to prepare and/or season the same foods.. which First Watch does not. It's straight up diner fare that just tastes bland, under-seasoned and frankly, uninspired . The coffee is alright, nothing fantastic, but it does taste like coffee. The prices are decent, the service OK and the atmosphere is what you would expect. It's not terrible, it's just, I don't know, kind of just there. text: Definitely a "must see" while in Nashville. Parking was a little strange though. I would have thought that they would have had a parking garage. text: Downgrade! I'd be misleading people if I kept my four star review at four stars; my recent experiences with Chow's have been anything but. For starters, they won't take credit cards for orders under $20. Does take-out Chinese EVER cost more than ten dollars? I think not. Next, the food. Last Friday I defied Lenten mores and ordered the chicken with broccoli. At $4.50, there is no denying that this is a total deal-- until you taste the chicken. The uniformly flat pieces seemed suspect, and the taste was not good, no matter how much sauce was soaked through. The chicken itself was also minimal; the dish would have been more appropriately named, broccoli with chicken. Even though I ask every time I call, there is still no option of brown rice; just boring old white or fried. Surely I can't be the only person who wants brown? The "amazing chicken" was still tasty the last time I ordered it, and I've always been pretty happy with their wonton soup. When I'm craving one of these items on my lunch break, Chow's will suffice, but I'll be trekking to Han Dynasty for now on when I really want to get down with some good Chinese.

text: This is a really fantastic soup & sandwich place (or beer & sandwich), the breads are always fresh, same with produce and meat. text: My wife and I stopped in here about 3 weeks ago and had an amazing visit. I had the pulled pork sandwich which was towering with delicious pork. My wife ordered the chicken which was also a ton of meat. We didn't realize how much meat we'd be getting when we ordered so we also got sides. I had the scalloped potatoes and slaw and both were great. The slaw is made without mayonnaise and is excellent on top of the pork sandwich. The staff was fantastic to us. They had a fresh batch of mac & cheese come out of the oven so rather than throwing out the previous batch, they brought us full size sides of it for free (it was good too!). They're really friendly people and were soon told about their newest dessert experiment - white cupcakes with a cream cheese/nutella icing. They smeared the icing on the still-warm cupcakes and gave my wife and I each a free one to sample. Holy sonuva... they were awesome. Needless to say, we walked out of there bursting at the seams from all the delicious food laid in front of us. I'm sure we'll be making another trip there again soon.

text: Taco Bus looks just like you would expect it to. Originally there was a bus. It served tacos. Nowadays, it also has a building expansion added to it for seated dining. Came here on a Friday night for a bite before a night of drinking and general shenanigans. I had a burrito stuffed with conchinita pibil (seasoned pork), which would put any of the big burrito chains to shame. This thing was huge, flavorful, and a meal unto itself. Probably too much for a pre-drinking meal, but good god would it be amazing during the wee hours of the morning (open 24 hours!). Given, the part of town that the original Taco Bus is located isn't the ideal place you'd want to find yourself at 3-4am. Consider yourself warned. Also had a few sips of their hibiscus lemonade. Talk about pucker! Very sweet and very tart, it's enjoyable for those who want an instant sugar rush. Or need to be resuscitated. All in all, the Taco Bus is a great experience. If you're a Mexican food lover, give this place a spin. Enjoy!

text: You know for $9.99 + tax, it was certainly worth the buffet. Let me tell you, everywhere else in New Orleans is trying to rip off the tourists. $9.99 is a steal. I have already come back here twice just to eat because you can sample the creole stuff that New Orleans has to offer without breaking your wallet. I had samples of the gumbo, shrimp etouffe, jambalaya, sauteed greens and shrimp, mashed potatoes and gravy, asparagus, ice cream, fruit....etc. They had sweet tea, a staple of southern cuisine. Of course, they don't feel the shrimp for the shrimp cocktail :( I'd stay away from the Asian food as it doesn't look too appetizing. I would come back here again and again!

text: Oh No! Another meal at Yet-Another-Food-Network-Celebrity-Chef's Restaurant. But this one is good, and it's worth it - no kidding! But before we begin, six magic words: FRENCH FRIES, FRIED IN DUCK FAT! (more on that later) We were here for a late brunch on a Saturday and were desperately torn between the breakfast side and the lunch side of the menu. Ultimately, the table of four wound up mixing it up and taking a bit of both. The $25 fixed price brunch is an excellent value and they are flexible with substations, etc. To begin, a little bit of sparkling wine was perfect and their amazing in-restaurant wine shop has a wonderful, reasonable selection. A dry California Brut started us out, followed by a semi-sweet French Rose. Delicious. Being able to get up and choose your bottle from a their refrigerated wine cases is fantastic. A starter of warm Vichyssoise with grilled scallops was incredible. Warm, creamy and complex - perfect for a winter day. We followed that up with a bacon quiche (large portion, light, excellent crust) and a Funghi Pizza (light, earthy, with a perfect chewy/crispy crust). But what took the cake was two orders or hand-cut french fries, fried in duck fat. They could possibly win my "Best Fries of 2010" award (and I spent some time in Belgium, this year, btw!). Crispy, just greasy enough, wonderfully flavorful with a perfect Bernais sauce on the side. Simply amazing. (Note: These are not always available - check for times of the day). I wish I could get an order of these after a long night of drinking. All in all, excellent food in a trendy, casual atmosphere at a reasonable value.
label: POS

text: First off, THIS RESTAURANT IS NOT IN PAOLI. It is on route 3 in Newtown Square...now on with the review... Is this the best sushi in Philly? No. But it is very good sushi, and definitely the best choice in the area. I've never been disappointed when eating there, which is pretty often since it's nearby and our default "I don't feel like cooking" hangout. We usually sit at the bar, which is usually pretty crowded. Everyone there is friendly and the service is good. The non-sushi menu items are also great - I particularly like the Seafood Drunken. I definitely recommend it if you're in this neck of the woods.

text: Honestly, there's nothing much better during St. Louis summers than a free outdoor festival. And by golly, Schlafly is the local King of outdoor festivals! I've planned my share of outdoor festivals and attended quite a few as a vendor as well as a regular attendee, and I have to give Schlafly props for doing it right. They are organized, easy to work with and take care of both their attendees and their vendors. There's never a freak out moment from the organizers (and I love that "no one is going to die if X doesn't happen" mentality), they think of all of the necessary details (i.e., ice water available to all, plenty of clean port-o-potties, shaded tents) and their staff is well-trained to deal with crowded situations. Oh, and their events are fun! Sometimes I dread having to work a table at certain events, but never with Schlafly! This weekend's Pork Steak Championship was a good time! It was hot and sticky outside, but the staff made sure we all had plenty of water (and beer) and were entertained. I don't eat too often at The Bottleworks but I love the fact that a majority of their menu items are made from locally grown food. Last night I tried their pulled pork sandwich and it comes topped high with coleslaw. Normally I'm not a slaw lover, but this hit the spot after a long afternoon in the sun. And of course it goes well with a Summer Lager... Still haven't tried their beer in a can, but I'm sure that'll happen before the end of the weekend :) Great local company, fun festivals, accommodating staff. Love 'em!

text: Made a reservation here for 7:30 on a Friday and we were seated 5 minutes after arriving. The place was very full. The marinara sauce was good, but the calamari themselves were subpar, specifically they seemed very thin (possibly over cooked?). My entree was the penne puttanesca, which was good. My only complaint is that the anchovies which should be a large part of that dish were hardly noticeable. My wife got the rack of lamb special. The lamb was quite tasty, although her sides were unimpressive. The wine prices are all very good (at least by PA standards), and both wines are tried were enjoyable. Neither will knock your socks off, but I'd order them again. We sat close to the bar and noticed some homemade limoncello being served. I did not get a chance to try it, but I like the idea at least. The service was kind of hit or miss. Our waiter was very friendly, he was just very hard to find, sometimes disappearing for long stretches. Overall, everything about the place had some positive and also some negative aspects. I would not be against returning, but its not too high on my list.

text: I went to this place 2 years ago and I couldn't stop kvelling about it. Present day-2010... We went yesterday on the spur of the moment. Well alot changed in 2 years! The place had only one other couple when we arrived. The staff was just sitting around waiting for peeps to arrive. We were greeted and seated cordially. We weren't dressed up and this place is pretty fancy so I guess they pre-judged us. If they only knew how much $$$$ we spend on restaurants on a daily basis they prob would've made a better effort. This place is a byob so Sid ran down to the local State store a few seconds away but we wanted to put in our order first so we'd have food on our plates by the time he came back with the wine. They didn't come over until i had to tell them to! Also, what's the deal with the half a slice of bread? They deal out just one time while we're waiting for our food. Sid got back and still no food. I'm starving and the bread was really good. So I waited for another serving; but no dice. I finally broke down and asked for another and told them to keep my plate full until my food came. This girl likes to eat and I'm not afraid to announce it. So the guy came over and dealt me out another half o slice again. Well our first course finally came. I got the parsnip creamy soup and Sid got the tasting menu. Eh my soup wasn't great. Sid's oysters came late. Then my entree, breast of chicken - too salty and not what i expected from this place. Not to mention the lack of announcing each course for the tasting menu. We've done many tastings and everyone that I've been at always announces each platter when they serve it. Its kinda nice. but not here. They just left the tasting menu on the table for Sid to read, cuts down on the announcing they figured. I don't think I'll be back here. What a shame. This place used to rock in service and food.

text: If you like getting tortured this is the place for you. I went in two days ago to get a pedicure because someone had given me a gift card. The woman doing my pedicure was not paying attention. Instead of filing the callous on the bottom of my toe she filed the soft skin on the side. I wasn't sure how much a pedicure should hurt (because this was only my second time having one) but it got to the point where my eyes watered up and I screamed "stop! that hurts!" I looked down and she had filed a hole in my toe and it was bleeding. She started putting oil on it to make it stop bleeding. Luckily my friend had a first aid kit so I cleaned and bandaged the wound. I asked to speak to a manager and the man working there who spoke the most english said there was no manager. He said sorry as I gave him my gift card and limped away. I wish I could upload a picture to show what that woman did to my foot. It still really hurts and will probably scar. text: I'm still reluctant to give a one star review, as to me, a one star qualifies as an actual turd, on a plate, poorly presented, and only mildly tepid, not steaming. And alas, Italian food in much of south jersey, while no prize, is still slightly better than that. So naturally I'll recount my meal, so as to allow others to assess my assessment. Act 1: The Bread- When we arrive, the place is crowded. We see two open tables, one in a cozy corner and one next to the kitchen in the way of everything and everyone. Naturally, I expected to be seated at the decent table. Tragically, we were not. I have no idea why, as that other table remained empty throughout the night, and we were dressed rather nicely too i.e. not looking like cheapskates. We were quickly handed the bread however, awful mealy (as in only good for mealworms, I guess) bread. I'm not hopeful. Act 2: The Calamari- Tasted like popcorn chicken from KFC, except with squid. I like KFC's popcorn chicken, especially since it's $5 for a tub, not about $15 for a plate with overly sweet marinara sauce (calamari should always be with fra diavolo!!!!!!) that tasted akin to sugared tomatoes that were crushed and pasted. Act 3: The entree- Veal something, that they somehow made greasy, not overly flavorful either.....oh and cold too! Perhaps this was someone else's dinner? Our wait staff was fantastic in its attentiveness, so I don't think that it could have been an oversight on their part. On a final note, even considering my hardly warmed over meal, I could possibly give this place 2 stars, because we were not actually served fecal matter (see 1 star rule), what upsets me most though, is the fact that a place that markets itself as a higher end establishment, in substance, it isn't. In a smaller niche market, like Haddonfield, I suppose this goes tolerated by the masses interested only in appearances. In a place like New York, I'd be surprised in the landlord would even allow this establishment to even get to the point of actually opening up.
label: NEG

text: I made the sorry mistake of purchasing a bridal gown from Bridaltown. Upon getting engaged in January 2009, my first order of business was purchasing my gown. A friend of mine suggested that I try a bridal shop in PA because of the bargains to be had. She did a little internet searching and came up with Bridaltown. My friend and I took the almost 3 hour drive to the middle of nowhere to find Bridaltown. The sales manager/bridal consultant, Gail, was helpful and nice. However, when it was time to purchase the gown, the high pressure sales tactics of a used car salesman came out. Because I knew that my wedding was a 5 months away, and because I loved the gown that I selected, I regrettably gave into the pressure and purchased the gown. I also paid additional money to have the gown "rush delivered" and was given a "guaranteed delivery date of April 20th," which, had the gown arrived as promised, would have given me enough time to have the gown altered in time for my May 3rd wedding. As the weeks and months passed, I periodically called in to check on the status of my gown. Every time, I was blown off and told that "it will come in by the guaranteed delivery date." As that date drew nearer, I called practically everyday, speaking to everyone who works there, including the owner, Bill Titze. Virtually every call included an excuse of one sort or another - "the computers are down," "your gown is on the truck," "your gown is stuck in customs," "there is no one here today," "the manager is out and the owner/buyer is out," just to name a few excuses that I was given. My gown finally arrived on April 24th, beyond the "guaranteed delivery date." When I asked for a refund of my extra money spent for rush delivery, I was refused. When I requested same day alterations, I was not accommodated. Rather, I was told to "come back next week and we'll take care of you then." My wedding was just a week away, and the trip to Bridaltown and back was nearly a 6 hour ride, and they wanted me to come back two more times for fittings - they were out of their minds!! I had to take the dress elsewhere to be altered. I provided Bridaltown with several opportunities to remedy the situation, but they refused. As a result, I plan to file a Better Business Bureau complaint, a complaint with the PA State Attorney General's Office Consumer Fraud Division and possibly a lawsuit in connection therewith because Bridaltown needs to understand that it cannot continue to do business with the public in this manner. Bridaltown's main concern is not the customer, but rather the bottom line, and once they have your money they make it clear that they are not obligated to perform according to the contract (Bridaltown requires payment in full before it will place your order). The anxiety and emotional distress that Bridaltown has inflicted upon me over the past several months, and especially the last several weeks, was not worth the few dollars that I thought I'd be saving by purchasing my gown there. I would not recommend this store to my worst enemy. Stay away!!
label: NEG

text: It is my own opinion that servers at tapas bars are paradoxically the most pretentious people in the world while simultaneously the most patient people in the world. They are the most pretentious because if you're going to work at a tapas bar you probably first know what a tapas bar is (sadly, everyone doesn't) and if you're going to put any effort in being employed at one you're going to have to know all the details of the food that makes up the interesting flavors on every small dish...you're also probably much more into wine than the average person... They are the most patient because, as stated previously not everyone knows what a tapas bar is, and if you last very long at a tapas bar you're going to eventually have to get used to calmly explaining the concept of "small plates;" a concept ('WHAT? I'm supposed to order multiple dishes and they're all going to be TINY???') that is lost on some people. The explanation is usually done best before ordering to avoid the shock of hungry unsuspecting restaurant-goers. The servers were fabulous, quick to fill our water glasses (I was, as always so thirsty), informative on beer selection (we opted out of wine because we were saving a bottle at the house to relax with after--PLUS, despite bottles being half off on Monday nights, it was still rather expensive), answered all my questions on the dishes ("Are the empanada crusts really sweet?"), put sauces on the side at our request, snuck me a printed menu at the end of dinner (I had asked if it was online, but our server wanted to make sure I had a paper copy)...the whole experience was great. The food was AMAZING. SOOO delicious. Every single bite. I had olives (one of my favorites) to start. The beer was Alahambra Black Lager was amazing. We shared: -Patatas Bravas -The Vegetariano Bocadillo -Queso de Cabra Cocinado -The Berenjena con Lentejas Empanadas I didn't think there were going to be enough vegetarian options to make a meal, but there were...and I was stuffed afterward. The ambiance of the place was great. Not too dark, but not at all bright, and great long square bar with dried roses hanging all around it. The bar was just starting to get hopping (in a wine bar kind of way) with people meeting friends and buying half bottles as we were leaving (around 9pm) I'm so glad we chose Bar Ferdinand.

text: Going to the Fox for me is always such a treat. So, the last time I went to the Fox, it was to take my husband to see Wicked. I've seen it already and while it's become a little too popular for me, I knew it was something he'd enjoy because it's such a spectacular show to see live. The show did not disappoint - in fact, it was better than the first time I saw it with the original touring cast. But, I'm not here to Yelp about the show, amazing as it was. I realize that the ushers are there on a volunteer basis. My mom did it for a season or two. They're not getting paid and they often have to sit through the same show several times before it finally moves on (and not all the shows they sit through are as entertaining as you might think...my mom sat through Phantom of the Opera FOUR times. I would have died.) HOWEVER. The ushers that were working the show on Sunday, June 27 (at 2:00 pm) probably should have paid me back for my tickets. Clearly stated in every program, on lots of signs throughout the theater, on your tickets, and as GENERAL THEATER ETIQUETTE, people should expect to have to wait for a pause in the action to be seated if they show up for the show after it's already started. Then WHY, are ushers seating people while this show has already started, blocking the views of those of us who DID bother to arrive on time, and shining flashlights (which are supposed to be pointed to the ground at all times anyway) in MY FACE?! It's when stuff like this happens, that I just freaking wish the ushers would use a little common sense and perhaps take that moment to educate people on a little theatre etiquette. Don't even get me started on the Muny (i.e. it is never okay to SING ALONG with the actors onstage). This time around at the Fox I wasn't sitting in the best of seats, so had I been paying a little more, I probably would have complained. But, attention to everyone - it is RUDE to show up late for a show. Just like baseball, you're to wait for a pause in the action before you make your way to your seat. It's also rude to talk during a live performance. Sure, in a place like the Fox, the actors can't hear you, but I paid money to hear them, NOT YOU. I adore the Fox, I swear I do. I'll be going there for years to come and hope to bring my children there some day (once they're old enough to follow the rules above). But, I'd be lying if I said my last experience there was my favorite. Great show. Not-so-great ushers and patrons. Oh well.

text: I have experimented with Szechwan peppers in my home kitchen but stopped one afternoon after thinking I had damaged myself - or more specifically, my tongue. I was like a phosphorous flare had gotten mixed in with my peppers and into my mouth. The reason I bring this up is that last night, at the Han Dynasty, I relived that experience. Times 1000. At one point, there was a sparkler in my mouth. I turned to my wife and to the woman next to me and asked what was going on. They both had a similar experience but not as strong -- probably because they were smarter and did not grab the piece of chicken with the large spice coated skin on it. Weirdly, if I took a drink of beer, the experience stopped momentarily - and then came back. This continued for about 10 minutes, then went away. Or it was the endorphin buzz that took me elsewhere. When I talked with Han about the spice in the chicken, what it did to my tongue - and the faith I relied on to tell myself I was OK, he said there is no reason to worry, because "it is all natural". I felt like saying yes... box jellyfish is natural too. But I didn't. I can't cover everything about the tasting dinner we enjoyed, so just let me say it was wonderful. But not for everyone. Those that love it are part of the club of adventurous eaters that want to explore authentic, undiluted cuisines and experiences. So maybe we had to take the first step to get wine & beer glasses, but I didn't mind. The water glasses were always filled and the foods kept coming. And at the end, Han came over with take out containers for any leftovers. One last word about the spice and heat level. I love spices. I grow chiles. I love heat as a dynamic element in food as long as it isn't the only objective. And in my opinion, it was not the only objective here. This clearly shows that this restaurant manages to maintain that delicate balance of spice and taste that attracts Indians and Americans alike. It is a BIG DEAL. Indians have a reputation of eating super-spicy food, and Americans have a reputation of eating super-bland food. A place that can manage to satisfy both palettes has got a good thing going, in my opinion. Let's talk about the food and service, shall we? I usually go there on the weekends during lunch. They have a lunch buffet everyday, and I get to choose from a good variety of vegetarian and non-vegetarian dishes. They keep rotating their menu, because I have not found the same collection of dishes everytime I have visited. But, there are a few items that are standard on the buffet menu, and I am not complaining :) They always serve 'naan' (bread) and Dosa (type of pancake, not sweet though) with the food, so you have something to eat the curries with. No rice is served though. My favorites are: Chicken Tikka Masala, Chili Chicken, Palak Paneer and Carrot Halwa. My girlfriend likes: Chicken Tikka Masala, Palak Paneer, and a few other vegetarian dishes. She says she could totally be a vegetarian in India :) The sweets/desserts are not the best, but they are still OK after a hearty Indian meal. I have had better desserts at Amber/Bombay Garden. The ambiance is relaxed. No dress code. I hate dressing up for food, so a thumbs up to this place for not having any dress code. The owner is a south Indian lady who is always friendly and talks to you nicely. One thing I would like to point out is that waiters/owners of most Indian restaurants are not the most courteous and will not necessarily greet you with a painted smile and pretend to be happy. The are usually grumpy, but its just the cultural difference. I was also like that when I first came to the US, but changed quickly when I realized that such grumpy behavior in public places is usually considered rude. Most Indians never understand that, and just stay the way they are. So, the service is OK, I guess. Certainly not the best, but you will not be disappointed. And last, but not the least - price. For the sheer number of dishes that you get to choose from, and the overall quality of the food, they charge a moderate sum of money. Around $9-9.50 on the weekends and maybe a dollar less on weekdays (pardon me, I do not remember the exact amount). So, bottomline - Should you go and at least try this place out once - YES. Should you fall in love with this place, like I have - That's your decision :)
label: POS

text: Bar Ferdinand has always been there for me when other establishments have fallen through. Standard Tap and North Bowl not doing happy hour yet? North Third and El Camino Real have too long of a wait? No one in your dinner party wants to try someplace new? Bar Ferdinand has been there for me. I think that if you haven't done tapas before, Bar Ferdinand is a good place to start out. A little friendlier (in atmosphere and on the wallet) than Amada, this warm, sleek NoLibs spot has something for everyone. The menu contains everything from blueberry ale and fried octopus for the food-curious to Miller Lite and fried potatoes for the less adventurous. Everything is reasonably priced. I've been here a few times, and there are few misses among the hits. Cons: some of the plates are awkwardly and sporadically spaced; some of the items on the menu were a bit "off" (a date- and cream cheese-stuffed pastry was just a little too cloying for me; a cold omelet wedge tasted a bit too much like, well, cold omelet). Pros: the majority of the meals are delightful in the combination of tastes and textures. My favorites, and staples for whenever I go there, include a perfectly assembled cheese plate, as well as these membrillo-manchego-apple foam-walnut sauce skewers. Bar Ferdinand should also be notable for being one of the few places in NoLibs a) that does not require yelling in order to be heard and b) has anything remotely resembling navigable space.

text: After this meal I can honestly say that I understand Plato. Here is the punchline for those of you into the whole brevity thing--noble is good. It's Meme good. It's Amada good. The drinks and the food kick serious ass. Ok onto the story. There are so many ways I can go with this review. I can talk about how they have a rooftop garden for herbs and veggies and the stuff is so fresh it's like a punch in the face from nature. I can talk about how they really know how to make a drink. Their bartenders make mixing a drink look like a lost art. I can talk about really great decor and chairs that effortlessly glide on the concrete floor. No, I want to talk about philosophy. I remember sitting in high school and learning about the differing viewpoints of Aristotle and Plato. The Plato one was cool because it talked about a chair. He said that while there are many chairs in existence, all these chairs are a mere impression of the one "ultimate chair." This we can think of as the abstract chair. This abstract chair is the perfect embodiment of what a chair should be. All real chairs (instances) are an interpretation of the one abstract chair. How does this have anything to do with Noble? The Pan Roasted Chicken. I never eat chicken when I'm out. I'm always drawn toward more exciting things. Previously, chicken was the tofu of meat to me. I took a chance however on Noble's Pan Roasted Chicken and it brought me full circle. If there is a perfect chicken dish in the universe, they have duplicated it. It's almost like the universe was going to explode, but it didn't. This was a breast of chicken, with crispy skin and a moist inside. It tasted like chicken should taste (in the ideal sense) and if that wasn't enough, there was a little piece of chicken sausage on the plate too. If that wasn't enough, the pieces of the breast were cylinders themselves (as a nod to the chicken sausage) If that wasn't enough, it was over escargot, bacon and broccoli rabe. Hallelujiah!! Holy s&*%!! Where's the tylenol? My first course was the white chilled asparagus soup. It had a very dramatic presentation and it tasted incredible. There was some kind of garnish in the bowl already when the waiter poured it in. I made sure to mix it up before I nomed it. For dessert, we shared the Milk Chocolate Parfait. Two things of note here. 1. Rosemay caramel - if this meal wasn't amazing enough, they put rosemary in caramel. I mean cmon. Awesome. 2. It was just enough dessert to maximize my enjoyment of the meal and not send me teetering over the edge into the full zone. I think this place is just so amazing. It's not an everyday kind of place but it's not snooty enough to be one of those special occasion places. It's really in its own category, which is just fine by me.

I don't expect to be treated like royalty, nor do I want to. I just want it to be a non factor in my day - get in, get out, and forget about it. The first time I was here, I didn't have the physical coupon, but it was on my phone. The Princeton people told me all I had to do was show them my phone coupon and my card and it'd be ok. But here, the lady stated that they can't do that bluntly. I just said to myself, well, ok, whatever. I came back in today. I had purchased some treats yesterday for my dog. I then got an email stating that all treats were 25% off. I decide to go back and buy some more treats to take advantage of the discount. I first go to the front and ask if they do price adjustments. The cashier said no, so I returned the items, only to buy them again. So after that went through, I grabbed the returned items, then grabbed 3 or 4 more bags of treats. After getting through the scanning, the same lady that I had encountered the first time asked the cashier "is this the guy that returned those items?" He said yes, and then she looks at me and says "I'll let you do this one time, but next time, you can't return items to get a discount. We don't do that." End of glaring. I thought to myself, am I getting reprimanded for purchasing items from your store? I knew I was paying more by coming here, but I figured I would help a small local business on items like this where it is a few dollars different. text: Went here for Valentine's Day. First of all, if you are going to have a special menu and close down all the other parts of your menu, don't lie about it. When we call, tell us about it, put it on your website, and don't tell us that everything will be available when it's not. Had the single most sub-par experience in a restaurant in stl. The staff was definitely the B-list. The service was atrocious. Who in their right mind announces your wine price so that every other patron can hear? That is, after you rummage through a closet on top of us searching for the wine, can't find it, and just chose another and told us precisely how much it cost in an out-door voice. Thanks, we came here to be judged by the other patrons, whose heads all visibly swiveled at the announcement. Also, who runs out of bread? And if you DO run out of bread, why would you leave the bread plate, butter knife, and other bread service accoutrements out? And, upcharging for beef (not even filet mignon - short ribs and something else not expensive) just seems to be nickle-and diming. It's not lobster. It's not even filet, and not, god forbid Kobe or Wagyu. It's shortribs for crying out loud! Running out of half the menu is bad. Especially at 8pm. Having the rest of that menu be less than tasty is also bad. It was also clear that SOME of the menu items in the stuff they had was running out and they were trying to save up. Part of the reason this is truly unacceptable is that for Valentine's Day you have reservations - 100% booked reservations WEEKS before V-Day. If you can't order correctly when you know exactly how many patrons will be in, that's a problem. It's a problem when the service is so bad the waiter apologizes at the end of it. It's a problem when everything tastes like it was sort of nuked because you have you B-game here. I understand Vday is a captive audience, but come on - we certainly won't be back and we certainly won't be entertaining guests here again. They may have gotten a pretty penny out of us once, but they certainly made it so that they'll never get a repeat customer out of it.
label: NEG

text: Well, last week, I went here cause it was just too cold and I wanted some hot spicy brothy jjigye in me. When I asked if I could get the soup wrapped (I didn't want to eat it all), the soup was carelessly poured into the container right in front of my eyes so that it made a huge spill over the table. And cause he didn't think to wipe it at all, he just looked over how it made a mess on the plastic bag as he put it in. I asked for napkins and cleaned it up. Really, I should've just said I'll do it from the start. It is such a shame. It's in such a good spot, and can be so much better with just a bit of care. Whenever I go to this restaurant, I leave feeling bitter that I've wasted money (as I'm sure it shows here). I think just getting their lunchboxes or sushi, selectively chosen (or with luck), is the way to go, if you end up going to this place. Don't think you'll get a decent Korean dish... text: I am a wine lover, but by no means am I a wine snob. So I want to make it clear that I fully concede to more knowledgeable folks out there that maybe Chaddsford wine isn't that good (comparably); maybe it is overpriced; maybe the winery is just a tourist trap. Etc. However, any place that makes a Spiced Apple wine is pretty much going to get 5 stars from me. That's just how I roll. I had been wanting to visit this winery ever since we lived in Chicago, where we had two friends who loved the Spiced Apple wine so much they would order it by the case and hoard it away in their pantry. The fiance and I finally made a trip out today for the Harvest Festival. First of all, this is the stuff perfect Sundays are made of. A scenic drive, perfect weather, live music, etc. So I was already happy before we started the tasting. Second of all, the tasting seemed like a pretty good deal to me -- there were 10 varieties to try, compared to six at our next stop on the wine trail -- couple that with the fact that I got to finish everything the fiance didn't like, and I was pretty happy by the time we left. As others have said, we preferred their whites over their reds. And the sweet/seasonal wines were definitely the best of all. My favorites were, of course, the Spiced Apple (served warm. awesome!) and the Sunset Blush, another sweet wine; I also liked the 2006 Pinot Grigio. I didn't LOVE any of the reds but I liked the 2006 Merlot quite a bit -- it was spicy. The Niagara tasted exactly like grape juice, which reminded me of communion, so that was interesting. All in all, I had a fantastic time and I'll definitely be back. Plus, it's fun to buy local!

The taste of the meat and barbecue sauce overpowered it though, so the pepper did not have that much of an effect. Very interesting place, and great food. It was easily the best barbecue I've ever had, and you should definitely take a walk around the Museum if you have time. I will not miss out on this place next time I'm in Tucson.

They wouldn't take us until she was there and kept pulling groups from behind us in line. So she arrived in five minutes and had to wait again in line anyway. I get that you can't just hold empty tables, but that wasn't the case, and we explained nicely. Losers. There are too many places for good oysters (like Drago's) to waste time with Acme's shtick.
label: NEG

text: I really wanted to like Raven. Seems like a lot of people have. I came on a Friday night for a friend's birthday celebration but had to wait out in the cold for a good 20 minutes as the place had a "one in, one out" policy going on. The bouncer creepily asked the girls in front of us if they were wearing sexy underwear. Not cool. So we finally get in. The party was going for sure, but the music was just AWFUL. The DJ must have thought the music was awful as well, because I don't think he played a song apart from Cee Lo's "F*ck You" for it's entire duration. There were more creepers than fun people in the crowd. The saving grace was that the birthday girl was so drunk that she'd have a good time anywhere. I'll only come back to Raven if I'm drunk enough.
label: NEG

text: Storyland is a great place for kids to see their favorite nursery rhymes brought to life. You can climb on a fire truck , go down the dragon slide, and stand inside a whale's mouth.
label: POS

text: We came here for lunch on a Saturday because it seemed kid-friendly. I got the Santa Fe sandwich with portabello mushroom and it was alright. The sandwiches come with a side and my salad was a good third of my plate, which I appreciated. My nephew got a side soup and it was so salty and pretty much inedible. The entree salads are very large and so are their appetizers. The service was not very good, however, probably because at lunchtime on the weekend they only had one waitress and one busboy. It took us a long time to get our check and pay which was annoying since we were a party of five plus two young children.
label: NEG

text: Terrible. Maybe it's the New Yorker in me but I don't understand why you would name your place Bridge and Tunnel on purpose. Oh, and cold, salty salty salty pizza ... no thanks.
label: NEG

text: The first time I ate here, I was pleasantly surprised by the amount of meat on the cheesesteak and cheese fries are so good! Well I only ate a half of sandwich since I ate 2 chicken sandwiches from Chick-fil-a earlier. haha The reason why it tastes so good, is the bread is fresh and so is the meat. And the cheese sauce just tastes so damn good. Well I like it so much I went back 2 more times while in Philly. Once you go there you get the hang of ordering. And I like the fact you get your food fast. Like another yelper said, they are like the soup nazi, but if you know what you want and order it right, there are no issues. I've yet to get sick from eating there, but every since coming back to Cali I've yet to eat anything called a Philly cheesesteak here.

text: Had high expectations for this place...a mixed experience at best. My wife grew up in Rome so her palate is great for discerning good Italian food. Risotto alla crema di scampi was a highlight...excellent sauce and delicious prawns. Sadly the veal piccata was tough and had lots of gristle...yuck. The grilled frutti di mare was another disappointment. Everything was overcooked and dry. The broccoli was mushy and the various clams, mussels were shrunken like a cashmere sweater you accidentally stick in the dryer. I'm sure they upcharged on the check as well. All of the entrees were 6 or 7 bucks higher than on the website. Dessert...too disappointed to try. Had a much better meal at Olio e Limone.
label: NEG

text: way to over priced for something really not that special. Maybe if you were walking past and you wanted something semi-healthy but they don't move that fast on your order and the gentlemen that i dealt with had some sort of sense of entitlement for working at the pita pit.... maybe just a bad day but still over priced.

text: One of my new favorite stops for good food and great beer. But especially beer. This place is all about the beer. Their amazing and ever changing selection is available in draft, growler and bottle form so you can enjoy it in the restaurant or at home. Their 7 fridges are arranged by area so if you're in the mood for a particular style of beer, it's easy to explore and find a new brew. There is always new beer to check out and the employees are friendly and ready to share their expansive knowledge. The food is wholesome, tasty and well made. Their simple breakfast options, for example, rival some of the best diners in the area. If you are in the mood for a quick and inexpensive dish, they're a great place for that as well. There are even great options for vegetarians that extend beyond salads.
label: POS

text: Donate a bike...save a kid. Many inner-city youth can not afford a bike of their own. Completing a course in bike safety, maintenance & repair earns them a refurbished bike & a helmet. To finance this, they take in old (adult) bikes, refurbish & resell them at a reasonable price. All bikes are thoroughly checked out & repaired by certified mechanics who donate their time. They also sponsor events such as the one that took place a few weeks ago; The "Cranksgiving Day" Food Drive. Feel better about yourself both physically & mentally...donate an old bike, or buy a refurbished one.
label: POS

text: Twenty years ago Delsa's had outstanding ice cream. The new shop has been cleaned up and has very nice indoor and patio areas. Unfortunately, the ice cream is not very good. The strawberry is bright bubble gum pink with no chunks of real strawberries in sight. It tasted as bland and artificial as it looked. The chocolate only had a mild taste of chocolate. Both flavors were not very creamy either. Even a chain like Cold Stone has better ice cream - and way more flavor options. Goody's is a much better choice in Boise.
label: NEG

text: DaVinci's was so good we had rated it best in Nashville on our first visit. We were craving it again so we went for dinner tonight and I don't know when I've been so disappointed. There was only one other table occupied when we got there and later one more table outside and not many to go orders going out the window. The service seemed a little slow based on the lack of business. I overheard the first table comment they never got their appetizers and the waitress' response "I think you'll be fine". Whether or not they had enough foo was not the point, the point was they didn't get what they ordered and that is never a good thing. She didn't offer to bring them. They had a lot of pizzas - probably 4 or 5 and it seemed each one came out separate with some pretty big lapses in between them. Something was amiss in the kitchen tonight. Based on the pizza we had tonight, I wouldn't even go back but because we had such good pizza once, we'll probably give it another try at some point. This really had nothing to do with the sauce, toppings and cheese - they were all what we remembered and fine. It was the crust. It was horrible. It had no chew to it what so ever. It was much too cake-like with a raw and cornmeal texture. Didn't feel or taste like it had yeast. This was not what we remembered. We barely ate half the pie and we ordered a large since we ate all of the medium last time. By the end of my meal, I was picking the toppings and cheese off the crust.
label: NEG

text: I am fairly knowledgeable in Pizza - i have eaten it at most New York hot spots - i make a pretty mean pizza myself. I am from Los Angeles and know the good, bad and great pizza that city has to offer as well. So when I moved to NOLA I was determined to find a great spot in the city for a pie.... I look for a few things. 1)Fresh Ingredients (IE buffalo mozzarella that is creamy and made that morning, kalamata olives, fresh cut pepperoni, tomatoes picked fresh off the plant etc) 2) thin, crispy crust 3)Sauce the goes to the ends of the entire pie 4)Red sauce that is not overwhelming yet adds that extra yummyness to the pie. 5)A pie where all the factors create a spectacular pie and one part does not overpower the other parts. So I have tried the local spots, Reginellis, Slice, Rocky's etc - still not satisfied and looking - My Roomie and I decided to try THEO'S as I have read many positive reviews and was anxious to finally fill my pizza void. The place is small and quaint. No wait staff - so we got in the "line" and ordered two Abita Amber's and The Arti-Garlic pie. The person at the register looked bored and annoyed. She did not instruct us to take a number, or that she would bring us our drinks.... she just looked at us and glared. My roomie FINALLY asked if she was getting our beers and if we picked the pie up at the counter. She said we needed to take a number and sit and it would all be brought to us. OK! We sat and patiently waited for this hyped up pie.... the gal at the counter switched personalities and was now super sweet... She brought us the Arti-Garlic and even gushed how she wanted to sit down and have a slice. First bite was off putting - So much artichoke flavor - in fact that is all I could taste - I continued to eat it started removing the artichoke pieces. It wasn't horrible but it was not what it was made out to be... First off I think it needs red sauce - the olive oil and garlic seemed absent. I could not eat more then one slice as it wasn't tasty. I will try them again but I will make sure I try a pizza with red sauce. I just won't be rushing over there...
label: NEG

text: What an excellent experience. The Scottish Arms offers an authentic (for what I hear) menu of Scottish faire. Our party had a variety of dishes from the Cock a Leekie Pie (excellent, rich soup-like dish), Double Cut Pork Chop (GREAT raspberry sauce), and Fish & Chips (Haddock with a 5 beer batter). Everything about the experience was wonderful as well, even the kids enjoyed the food. Also, the atmosphere in the dining room as nice as well, clean, great service and they were accommidating. We didn't try the whiskey's, but the selection was very impressive.

text: I should be more generous with the stars as it's a Motel 6 not the Four Seasons, and paying only $42 should reduce expectations significantly to account for a lack of Do Not Disturb signs, and the fact that internet is not available in every room. text: On my recent trip to Reno we visited The Imperial during the Wine Walk. The interior was very spacious and comfortable... booths and tables EVERYWHERE that seemed very private. The beer selection was extraordinary. On the back wall was a HUGE blackboard with all the beers listed. I counted 55 ranging from Pabst blue ribbon at $2 and various others I had never heard of at $13. We ordered a pizza with artichokes, garlic, spinach and red peppers and Asian chicken wings. The pizza was a wonderful lunch choice; light yet satisfying. The Asian chicken wings were amazing. Sweet and spicy with no mistaking the Asian flavor.

text: I find it funny that people think this place is so vegetarian friendly. Not that it isn't. But they are really no more so than anywhere else. Other than salads (and almost every restaurant has salads that vegetarians can eat) there are about two choices. The veggie pita / melt (which is successfully passed off as two choices when it really should only merit one). I find this pita melt combination quite bland to be honest with you. So I usually go for choice #2 the "beans & three" plate (meaning beans and a choice of three sides). The food is good and healthy but the service is slow. There is always a considerable wait even when the dining room is empty. But if you do want something healthy this is a good place to stop. Its also fairly affordable.

text: A rare fusion joint that has both good food and good service. As is the case with most fusion places the apps really stand out: The crab avocado wrapped in salmon with capers was very good. As was the grand marnier prawn and peach dish. Outstanding combo. The main dish came across as a really big appetizer with less adventure, it hugged a little close to the coastline as a skipper would say. The Lamb chops were above average. If I came here again it would be for an early dinner I would get a bunch of the apps and a bottle of wine. Their wine list is full of quality selections, and the staff actually knows of the wine and can give specific feedback as to what is what. They had a bunch of wines from Spain, Portugal, and Argentina that were quite good. The Pinot Noir from Argentina is what I had. Lovely.

text: Heard about this place in a tour book about New Orleans, supposed to be the best po-boy in town. Not really impressed. The food was OK, the line to get it ordered was pretty long, and the delivery of the food after you ordered it left a lot to be desired. Finding a parking spot nearby is a problem. Nice atmosphere, but not worth a retrun trip.

text: What happened to the days of men dressing like men? I'm not a Cowboy or a steel worker, but there isn't a thing in this place that I would be caught dead in. Overall it's great for teens and women, but that's about it.
