text: My dogs love Country Haven Kennels. And for some reason I haven't figured out yet, Country Haven seems to love them. I first took my dogs to Country Haven last year. I had been using another kennel that took good care of them, but that kennel had this infuriating policy of a 2-day minimum charge, 3 on holidays, even if you had multiple dogs sharing a single run (they had a, I think, like 4% discount for the second dog: woo, don't spend it all in one place). I had finally had enough when I needed to board my 2 hounds for a single night in a single run for one night on a holiday weekend; their policies meant I'd be paying a very slightly discounted 6 night charge for the 1 run/1 night/2 dogs that I actually needed. And so I went shopping for a new kennel--one that wouldn't steal all my money with insane minimum-charge policies. I found Country Haven shortly after it had been sold to a new owner. Her name's Casey and she was clearly SO THRILLED to have this business, like it was her dream to be a kennel lady and it finally just came true. She also had a rescue dog or two who needed crash space chilling out at the kennel the first time I visited, and more or less every time I've been back since---I don't know where she finds them but she's clearly a big old softie where a homeless dog with a sad story is concerned. You can tell she really loves animals. She's always very sweet about mine, even though they're kind of hyper and loud and obnoxious: I adore them but I have to, they're mine, you know? Casey is always *very* good-natured about it when my dogs show up and make total asses of themselves... as they always do. One of my dogs has to get a bunch of different medicines or she breaks out in rashes, which is how I know she actually does get it when she goes to Country Haven. That's really important. And lastly, Casey's been really nice a couple of times about scheduling snafus. One time several months ago I boarded the huskies to spend a weekend in NYC: that weekend ended up being one of last winter's endless snowpocalypse dramas, and a delayed train home plus unplowed roads meant that I showed up to get the dogs like half an hour after the kennel was supposed to have closed. I can tell you for a fact, no one would have given me even 5 minutes of leeway at their old kennel. She didn't even charge us the "special arrangements" fee. And! Last month I boarded the dogs to go out of town for a week. On what was supposed to be my last night there, I got a phone call from a friend with an emergency, so instead of sleeping that last night, I was all Action Superhero Girl, and long story short, I slept right through Country Haven's evening hours when I was supposed to be picking my dogs up. I showed up the next morning as soon as they opened, and Casey was super chill about it, AND didn't charge me for the extra night, which is kind of amazing. So, you know. I'm a happy camper and so are the dogs. Only downside I can think of is that I got spoiled with the OCD levels of meticulous grooming at my last kennel---it's not quite as good at Country Haven. It's not enough of a thing to make a difference, though. And their weekend office hours are kind of limited, but it's kind of dumb to complain about that when, like I say, they're willing to make special arrangements for a fee that they didn't even charge me when they should have.
label: POS

text: We dropped in before the symphony and were able to sit down without a reservation on a Saturday night - I certainly appreciated that. Also the drinks were good, they have some of our favorite Asian beers and I enjoyed the blood orange mojito. But if I were to dine at Chew Man Chu again I would want to drink several of them before the food is served. Not surprisingly, this restaurant is not great. The food reminds me of suburban strip mall fare, very sugary and fatty. We had the calamari which was dressed with a nice spicy sauce, but not as crispy as one would like. We also ordered orange beef (dreadful), miso ramen (meh) and Pad Woon Sen (the best of the bunch). My son enjoyed the ramen and this is definitely a menu that appeals to children, though the atmosphere is a big 'lounge-y' for kids. Service is difficult to evaluate. Our server as very sweet and enthusiastic but seemed very high strung and I felt badly for her as she attempted to explain the menu. Her delivery would be great for people who do not eat authentic Chinese, Vietnamese, Thai, Korean foods and are unfamiliar with the dishes. Also the service seemed to be geared to people in their early twenties: Me:This mojito is delicious. Server: I know RIGHT?!? I felt like I was trapped in an episode of 16 And Pregnant or something! Still she was pleasant and pretty efficient, and that is what really matters. The truth is that if we find our selves looking for a bite before the theatre or a concert again, we may well stop in again. But it will be for the convenience rather than the food.
label: NEG

text: I was a little hesitant to go here as the restaurant shares the building with a laundromat, but it was pretty outstanding. I may be a lightweight, but I got blasted off one margarita here. Don't expect anything less than extremely strong and extremely big (12 ounces is a pretty good sized 'rita), not to mention you can't beat a $4 drink that leaves you practically falling out of the booth. Though I was toasted by time my meal arrived, I was also blown away at how quickly we got our meal. The vegetable fajitas were great, though it would have been nice to get a couple more tortillas. And you can't beat all you can eat chips and salsa. I also enjoyed all the bizarre, pseudo-Aztec-Harlequin art on the walls, though I don't think it was meant to be as large of a joke as I made it. I will be back to Mi Ranchito next time I'm ready to get my Sunday-afternoon drink on.
label: POS

text: We went for walk and stumbled across this pleasant looking trattoria in Queen village. The service was spotty but the waiter was very pleasant when available. The sign posted outside said it was pizza night so we thought it would be a nice way to get a lite bite. We selected the Positano pizza which had carmelized onions, mushrooms and chicken in a light tomato sauce. What a mistake. The pizza was dry, the chicken was bland, the onions weren't carmelized and the dough tasted like it came from Shoprite. Although our taste for pizza revolves around Taccanellis, Mara's and Mam Palma's, which are the best of the best, this place is a far cry and ranks with the pizza at the Wachovia Center. Awful!
label: NEG

text: This place is extremely popular, and for good reason. The first I went (with my wife and two sons), the place was very crowded, even in the summer. Somehow the service still shockingly fast. Coffee was smooth and tasty, but the Mocha I had very little chocolate flavor. Wife had Chai, and thought was great. She also had smoked salmon and she loved it. Despite the fact that we could barely find seats, we still had a great coffee experience On my second trip, coffee very smooth but also rich. The iced mocha was pleasantly sweet, but still not strong on chocolate flavor. As I thought he would be hungry, I decided to share an order of French toast with son. The verdict: very good. Addition of strawberries and banana was a nice touch along with the excellent french toast and good syrup. The was service still lightning fast, so much so that my food came out before my drink was done being prepared. For excellent service, very tasty food, good coffee, and very good wifi, Bongo Java in the Belmont area should be on your short list coffee houses in Nashville.
label: POS

text: This weekend I placed a fairly large phone order at Chef Ken's. The young man who took the order told us it would be a 45 minute wait on the mac and cheese. We read such great reviews that we didn't mind the wait at all. So, 50 minutes later I sent my sister in to pick up the order. The chef explained to her, in a not so polite fashion, that he hadn't put our food on because everything is made to order to preserve freshness. I definitely appreciate fresh food but I just cannot understand why an establishment would accept phone orders if they won't prepare the food before your arrival. My sister forgot how long the order was going to take and didn't bother to ask the total. So I went inside very annoyed! I had placed the order at 5:03 at this point it was 6:18 and I had to get out of my car with a broken foot. But nevertheless, I was not loud nor disrespectful. I asked the young man at the register how much the order would be and how much longer it would take, he said $92 and "about five more minutes" I said thank you and walked away. As I was walking out the door the chef yelled across the room "Excuse me "SIS" is there a misunderstanding"? I told him how long I had been waiting for my food and that he should notify customers of his policies. He made no apologies but told me in a very loud and condescending voice that he has been doing business that way for 15 yrs. About ten minutes later, I got my food and left. After checking my order in the car I realized I hadn't received my sides. I went back in and was greeted with a very rude " Is there a problem?" Well little did he know I was purchasing the food for a tasting. (Which by the way the food was delicious.) He had such great reviews I was considering using him to cater an event with 125 people at Curtis Arboretum but if that's how he treat his customers he will never receive business from me nor my family businesses again.
label: NEG

text: great menu for all kinds, and spectacular service. i always stop by here if someone with me hasn't been yet. be careful not too get a super hard bread though!

text: Bicycle revolutions is my designated neighborhood bike shop. With a somewhat limited selection, and slightly higher prices, they're not my all time favorite. But, time after time, I find myself coming here because they're just so damn friendly and convenient. Brian is really great. I bought my first new bike (all the previous ones were hand me downs) here. At the time I didn't know much about what I was looking for. Brian helped me find a bike that fit correctly and was pretty much exactly what I was looking for. Six months later, I've learned a lot more about bikes. I would avoid buying a complete bike again, and instead build one myself. And I'm sure that Bicycle Revolutions could help me do that. But all in all, they're a great shop, and are largely responsible for getting me into such a wonderful activity. Oh and I just bought my helmet here! Good selection and they helped me find one that fit. Get a helmet :)

I don't know if they recently changed food brands or there is a chef in disguise in the kitchen but it was awful. It's a shame because I like the atmosphere in the bar area.

I've tried so many things here from General Tso Chicken, Orange Chicken, Beef with Brocolli, Lo Mein, Chow Mein, Mongolian Beef, Sesame Chicken, Honey Chicken, Fried Shrimp...If it's on the menu, I've probably tried it. Their food never tastes that great and the chicken doesn't really taste like chicken...I spent forever on New Years looking for another place to eat, but of course the Chinese place was the only one open. text: Went here after a stiff night at Vango TRYING to celebrate a birthday. We left, came here and the celebration really began. Cheap drinks, great music, mixed crowd, friendly staff, plenty of seating, room for dancing. Is there anything else you could ask from a place? Let's just say The Raven Lounge gives you the kind of morning you wake up laughing to, only remembering where you were because they gave you a business card before you left. Awesome time.

text: It sounds like the people reviewing this restaurant either hate it or love it. I recommend just going there and finding out what you like from the menu and sticking to it. I had a nice breakfast/brunch item that was basically eggs on a piece of toast with a slice of ham and it was fantastically delicious! I had a beer as well and that meal was one of the best meals i have ever had. i could have died happy after that meal. The service was a bit slow but fine because i was drinking my beer and reading the paper. The waitresses are also really gorgeous there! This is a great place to take a friend and just sit at the bar and have a meal and a chat.

text: So...this place. We went here for brunch. And we brunch all over the city. A different place every Sunday. But this place, ugh. We got there at 12:30ish. They were serving a brunch buffet for $22 but if you wanted to sit outside you had to order from the menu (totally fine). We wanted to sit outside, but then they informed us that we would have to wait because they couldn't give us the lunch menu until 1pm. Ok fine - but can we sit? No, you can't sit. Not until we can serve the lunch menu, wtf?! The whole place was crawling with unnecessarily pretentious staff (you're on a river and it's green - come on) who could not believe that we would be persistent and ask to be seated at the restaurant where we would be spending nearly $200 within an hour or so. The food was mediocre. The setting was nice - white umbrellas against the river and deck. The inside looked big, but dark. Our waitress was nice but not so happy with our request to move an unused umbrella to just partially cover our table of 13 people. I feel like I go out to eat almost every day. I travel all over. And I know when pretense is inevitable and somewhat understandable. Here it is not. I was entirely unimpressed. If it weren't for the serenity of the outdoor seating I think it would be a 1-star.
label: NEG

text: We love this place. Yummy coffee, tasty treats, and hearty sandwiches make Mugshots the place to go in Fairmount, no matter when you wake up. Although the hunger is satisfied, the wallet becomes increasingly more emaciated. We feel worse about our good food when we realize way too much of our hard-earned, starving-artist money has just disappeared. WOMP WOMP...If you ever hit the lottery, try the breakfast burrito, vegan B.L.T., B.L.T.A., or get some hot bagel action.

text: I just moved into the area and heard so much about Sidecar that I decided to give it a try. Why not, it's really close by! We had nachos, mussels and calamari. The calamari came with this sauce that tasted a little bit of bbq with tomato sauce, unusual but very good. The mussels were great and unique with tomatoes and salami. I thought the decor was quaint and welcoming and can definitely picture myself going back and bringing friends along. They had a great selection of beer, not just your typical miller lite/coors/bud. yuck. I think it would be great if they expanded. Will need to go back for brunch!
label: POS

text: I'm not much of a Malaysian food expert, but, hot damn I loved this place. I don't know whether Penang qualifies as "authentic" or not, but all I know is that Penang served up some of the most delicious food I've ever tasted. Hyperbole much? I don't think so. My dinner companion and I stepped in here on a frigid Tuesday evening. Although the streets were empty outside, Penang was buzzing with both conventioneers and locals. The space was quite large with a quick turnover of tables, we were able to get a choice spot overlooking the open kitchen. It was a great atmosphere to browse the sprawling menu while sipping the complementary hot tea. Although the staff seemed a little frenzied, they were always prompt and polite. Our server was quick to take our appetizer order, so we started dinner with the following-- * Roti canai. These crispy Malaysian-style "pancakes" were delicious. They came with a curry sauce for dipping, which made for a decadent (albeit messy) start to dinner. * Tofu satay. Massive tofu pieces crisped to perfection, served with a generous pile peanut sauce with cucumbers mixed in. This was probably my favorite item of the night. Next up, the entrees. We both settled for noodle dishes and ate family style, to maximize the opportunities for sharing-- * Chow kueh teow. Basically, these are rice noodles stir-fried in chili and soy and tossed with squid and shrimp. Although I'm not a seafood fan, I was completely surprised by how delicious this one was. The noodles were crispy and flavorful, and the dish didn't taste "fishy" at all. * Beef chow fun. A classic -- beef with flat noodles and sprouts. This was outstanding too. The beef was crispy and spicy, and nothing like the greasy-spoon beef chow fun that I'm used to. Four dishes -- and four home runs. Sounds like a five-star dinner to me. A five-star dinner that was also dirt-cheap (dinner for two amounted to a mere $20 + tip). Nice. No doubt I'll be back here the next time I'm in town.

text: Noble is one of the few restaurants in Philly which really does Restaurant Week right. After disappointing meals at Tangerine, Chifa and XIX over the past year, I'm really happy to have found a place that can actually prepare a decent meal despite the increased stress. Here's a breakdown of my experience: The Good: 1) The alcohol selection. The beer list is well selected and reasonably priced (12oz bottles are $4.75), ranging from local favorites like Yards Brawler to beers I've never heard of like Two Brothers Domaine DuPage. The one cocktail I tried was fantastic - I can't remember the name (next time I should really take notes) but it was a scotch based drink with lemon and dill and was exactly the type of drink I love. I'll be back for the bar. 2) The décor. It's almost worth going to Noble just to check out the bubinga bar. I can't imagine how much it must have cost. I didn't get a chance to go upstairs, but after reading other reviews I'm sorry I didn't. 3) The dessert. The chocolate pecan pie was amazing, one of the best desserts I've had in Philadelphia. I'm surprised others were disappointed - I was truly impressed. The Less Good: 1) The service. Our waitress was pleasant enough, but there was a 20-minute dead zone between our first and second courses. All of us were staring at our empty drinks and plates, wondering where the servers were. Other than that incident the service was fine, and it was Restaurant Week after all, so I'm not taking away too many points here. 2) The non-dessert food. Some dishes were fantastic - the arctic char reminded me of a breezy day at the beach in June (in a good way) - but a few dishes missed the mark. I tried the fries that came with a friend's burger and found them to be underwhelming, and the cauliflower salad was flavorless aside from the cauliflower itself. Given that I'm a pretty skinny guy and I was hardly stuffed after four courses, I had to deduct a star for these couple of misses. All-in-all, I'd give the restaurant week experience a 5, despite the hiccups. It's only restaurant week for 4 weeks a year, though, and I suspect I'd be less satisfied if I was paying full price. Either my wallet or I would have left only half full, and the food wasn't quite good enough to justify either of those feelings. I will almost certainly return for drinks, though.

There are also many of the standard Indian foods, including freshly baked indian breads in the refridgerator units, a whole isle of chutneys, pickles, and curry powders, and some spicy (and simple) snack foods like spiced chick-peas, more flavorful and healthier than most American snacks. text: This place is terrible. If you like this pizza you must really hate food. This has to be the worst pizza in the Royersford, hell, Philadelphia area. To use corn meal, which is not commonly used in making a good Italian pizza, is a horrific idea. The main reason you use corn meal is to keep the pie from sticking to the pizza peel. Penny's saturated the dough in corn meal then pounded more of this god awful substance into it whiles stretching it out. (side note: if you reheat this pie later on that corn meal will give the pie a disgusting cardboard taste with an unpleasant after taste.) After they ruin the dough, they do make an attempt at redemption but putting a good amount of cheese on the pizza. I can't knock that, you will never complain about too little cheese. Then to finish of this insult to good pizza everywhere, they dump insane amounts of obnoxiously sweet sauce all over the top of this pizza. I love Boardwalk style pizza and love sweet sauce, but this place kills everything good about both of those things. I swear the only people that like this place is older people that have delusional memories of this place from when they were kids. But come on, what child has a palette that as an adult we would find edible?. They offer pedestrian toppings and the menu is limited to Pizza and Stromboli's. Let's completely look past the creep old dirty house that is the shell of the restaurant and the lack of any customer service. I swear the attitude the employees had felt like they were doing me a favor buy making me this pizza. I can put all that aside for good food, but this place offers nothing in the way of quality or taste. It makes me question the judgement of those who would dare call this good pizza. As if this was not enough the final insult comes at charging $12.00 for a plain pizza. I will never go back and can't wait till this place closes. Why would any self respecting pizza connoisseurs eat this food? Penny's is back, but who cares!
label: NEG

text: I was in St. Louis for a wedding last weekend and we picked Sen Thai-Asian Bistro off of Yelp to try for Friday night dinner. We were staying in Union Station, but Dave convinced me we could walk, that it was only "a few blocks". It was far more than "a few blocks" and when we got there at 9:15, we quickly realized that they closed at 9:30 - this is a FRIDAY NIGHT mind you. We hemmed and hawed over what to do but realized the only other restaurant we'd seen on our journey was a chain pizza joint, so decided to beg them to let us order to-go. We walked in and they had that stricken look on their faces like WHAT? YOU WALKED IN 15 MINS BEFORE CLOSING AND EXPECT SOMETHING FROM US? I quickly assured them we did not want a table (though there were four or five parties in various stages of dining) and they quickly packed up our tofu pad thai and tofu-vegetable panang curry. Now maybe they thought we'd never had panang before and thought that tom kha gai with peanut sauce mixed in was close enough. Or maybe THEY didn't know what panang was, but this was no panang. For one thing it came in a soup container. It had enough baby corn to choke a donkey. Good heat though, I'll give them that. The pad thai was uninspired and the noodles were a very strange width and texture I'd never seen used for pad thai before. Its dark and romantic, so would be a good place for a date if you've never had thai food before and have low expectations.
label: NEG

They told me that my chili nachos would be right out, I corrected the server, that mine were not chili, but regular black bean nachos. He pretended like he just mispoke, but we all know that he screwed up the order. Everyone at the table was nearly done eating before I got my food. The server half-heartedly apologized for the mistake, but made no real effort to make up for it. text: Cleanliness: I've ridden train/bus systems in San Fran, Chicago, D.C. and NYC. Philly trains are generally(though not always) far more dirty than either San Fran or D.C. trains. They are on par or maybe a little better than the Chicago trains. I haven't smelled eau de homeless person very often here in Philly unlike in Chicago. Depending on the stop you get on/off of here in Philly you may encounter the smell of urine which is also part of my "fond" memories of Chicago mass transit. Somehow the City Hall station always smells of something and is really dirty. The Metro lines at DC are the cream of the train lines that I've ridden on. Clean trains, very clean stations, and friendly workers. Reliability: As far as SEPTA reliability, I"ve had fairly good luck with the Orange/Broad St. Line. However when I've switched over to go to West Philly, then the trouble starts. The trains that I've taken to West Philly may or may not be on time and may or may not have room. Not to mention there isn't enough seating for the masses that accumulate when the trains aren't on time. Service: Hands down, SEPTA workers have to be the surliest, most customer unfriendly of all the mass transit workers I've encountered. I've worked in service industry positions before so I know how people can be idiots, but still, there is a level of uncaring and downright hostility that exudes from the majority of the ticket takers I've encountered here. So far for me its been a mixed bag. I get to where I want to go, but I do feel like I need to take a shower after riding on some of the train lines. Not to mention having to swallow some anger after being treated like crap from ticket people.

Our server was friendly, with food suggestions, and wasn't pushy with drinks or following up. She introduced us to the other bartender when she took a break, and he not only held a great conversation, but informed us on the various whiskey's and gin's that they had! This place can't get much better. The cons (which aren't many), the food is more expensive than you would usually expect for a bar/burger joint, but it's not overly pricey, just don't go there expecting to spend 6 bucks on a meal! The only other con, is that the place is small, and it's becoming more and more popular so it's hard to get a seat. But it creates an awesome after work atmosphere. text: I had the extreme pleasure of visiting this organization's visual arts gallery yesterday when I had some free time before work. What a pleasant surprise. I discovered it through one of the few weekly free newspapers in Philly, and after having gained an interest in Chinese pop art over the past couple years, I'd see what some local and national Asian artists were up to. The exhibition, called Transplants, features sculpture, painting, photography, mixed-media/collage pieces, video art, and interactive travel art. There is quite a lot of lighting through the huge open windows at the front of the gallery. Who knows what the place looks like at night, but it's a loft/warehouse style gallery so I'm sure there's a "cutting edge" feel to it. I visited on Monday. Please note that the gallery does not usually open on Mondays, but the executive assistant was kind enough to let me in and set up all of the video pieces for me. Definitely quality service. I also got to meet the director, who personally greeted me as I browsed. In regards to size, there were about thirty to forty individual pieces in the one-room gallery. There was also a giant table that I'm assuming is used for special events, and there is a second, back-room that is probably used for the events as well. I hear that there was recently an open-mic for poets and performers. I recommend you check the place out. It's inconspicuous but well-worth the visit. The information provided on the featured artists is fulfilling, and there's a great sense of quality overarching the entire space.
label: POS

text: If I had to pick a favourite Starbucks in Edmonton, I think this one would be it. The only way to describe this setting is that it is wonderful. This is what a coffee place should be. It has a great setting and the building is nice also. It's an older brick building with tall arched windows and a high ceiling. It's a nice change from the modern-style Starbucks I'm normally in. I get the feeling that this place has been here longer than most of the Starbucks in Edmonton. It's a very relaxing location that is conducive to having a relaxing chat with a friend or avoiding the stress of the office. It's not far from downtown either. I just wish it was closer to home for me. I will now judge every other Starbucks I go to by this one. Busyness - It's pretty steady. Obviously it's a popular coffee place in this older neighbourhood. I get the feeling I was lucky to get the biggest table in the place. Noisiness - Aside from the occasional blender, it's generally pretty quiet. The music is at an acceptable level and I'm tucked away at the back, so I miss much of the traffic. Ambience - I understand this is called High Street and it's a great area just a short distance from 124 St. Power - The booths don't seem to have power but the other tables look to have power available. You may have to stretch a cord in some areas. I don't know if the patios ever have power. Free wifi - Yes, free wifi is available and works well. Staff - They're friendly as always. I got my coffee quickly as I usually do. I almost always order coffee, unless I'm at a Starbucks in the evening when I order passion tea. If it's got an 'O' on the end of its name, I probably will never order it. Seating - It's not a big place, but it's laid out well and it has a lot of seats. The prep area doesn't take up half the floor space, like it seems to in some places. There are 24 seats with two of them being comfortable armchairs. Those seats also include three great little two-seat booths. With one large table to work at, you'll easily fit four people. The outdoor patio is huge (nine tables) and on a hot day it would be really nice to enjoy sitting out in the shade of the huge trees (elms?) lining 125 St. Security - Seems like a pretty good area, but I'd still lock up the laptop or bring it with me when heading to the washroom.

text: It is what it is. This place makes a solid burger. We had the blue cheese and the peanut butter with loaded bake potato and alligator sausage gumbo. Meat is beefy, smoky, juicy and cook to exactly as we ordered (medium rare). Both are pretty much what we expected. The peanut butter works just fine, but they may have been a bit too generous, but hey, better more than you need than too little. Blue-cheese and bacon works like Laurel and Hardy, they may bicker and are different contrasts in taste, but you can't deny they compliment each other well. The bake potato had real bacon, lots of shredded cheese, butter and sour cream. Hard to mess up on a baked potato though. The alligator gumbo just sounds more exotic than it really is. The meat was a bit dry, and it could've used a bit more kick, but the flavor is there, and you can note the hints of onion, garlic, celery, among other spices. There's so many places to try around 'Nawlins, but if you're in downtown and want a burger, it's a safe bet to head down to Yo-Mama's.

The menu is extensive at first glance, but I quickly realized that at least half the rolls are available at dinner only. You will have access to the sushi basics however, including some really dynamite options like the rainbow roll. Since the prices are low, it's tougher than it sounds to get your $14 worth (the price of the all-you-can eat lunch). This is especially true because the rolls are ENORMOUS (8-10 pieces each!!!). I stuck to the nigiri for the better part of the meal, eating only the fish, and leaving the rice. The fish slices were not too thick and not too thin, and tasted fresh and tender. The pieces aren't especially generous, but you can get as many as you like. I highly recommend taking advantage of the free miso soup, and ordering any roll "spicy;" the chefs won't let you down.

text: I had one of my worst night's sleep ever at this hotel! It overlooks the 10 Freeway and you can hear the traffic from individual vehicles through the paper-thin walls all night. On the way out, I spoke to the manager and suggested he let guests have the option to choose which side of the freeway that they will sleep. text: I really, really wanted to like this place. In fact, it pains me to give it only 2 stars. The guy is not only a local legend and a national celebrity, but he lives in my spice cupboard, or at least his face does under the guise of "seafood magic" (wonderful seasoning btw). No one in the city has anything bad to say about him, and why would they? He pretty much single-handedly introduced a culture and cuisine to the rest of the world that had gone unappreciated much too long. And I am sure that at one time, when K-Paul's was still the no-reservation divey hole-in-the-wall with a line out the door, it was THE place to go in NOLA. But now . . . well, you see my stars. Here's why: the renovations with the white-tablecloth decor and high prices do not match with the food (in both quality and presentation) or with the service (felt like I was in a diner).There's a certain expectation when you pay $20-$35 an entree with your white wine and tablecloth and that expectation wasn't met. If, on the other hand, I was sitting at a formica table chugging a beer, being served by a gum-snapping waitress and paid half as much, I would've been very, very satisfied. Here's what we had: - Gumbo: I had gumbo probably 5 times while I was there, and K-Paul's was the worst. It was dark and oversalted. - Fried green tomatoes w/ shrimp remoulade: I actually liked this a lot. - Alligator sausage: Kinda like K-Paul's itself -- it was okay but at least now I can say I've tried it. - Blackened catfish: This was very, very good. I would recommend it. - Etouffee: It was pretty good. - Fried drum: It was okay. - Fried soft shell grab: It was okay. At this point, all the breading started tasting the same. - Bread pudding: Very good. - Sweet potato pecan pie: Good but not great. So overall, the food was just okay or even slightly below average. The presentation was terrible, but again, I wouldn't have cared if it weren't for the nicer setting and fine-dining level prices. Same with the service -- not very good given the enivronment. Am I glad I went? Sort of, because now I can say I've been, and sometimes as a tourist, that's all you really want. But as a tourist who during her visit was most looking forward to the food, I was severely disappointed.
label: NEG

text: Every time we go to Reno, we end up eating in the casinos. This time, I wanted to venture out and see what Reno really had to offer. The place itself looks like an old house, with the inside gutted out. The tables and chairs don't all match. Each table had vinyle table covers that don't get cleaned after each seating. The waiter (son) just comes by and uses the menu to dust off the table, and then hands you the menu after! Every time we would move in our seats, the table cloth would slide off the table. There is only ONE person running the outside, the son of momma. He is the busboy, waiter, host. I honestly feel horrible for him. The place is small, fitting about 50 people in it, but it was pretty packed on a Friday night at 8pm. So you can imagine how the service is with just one person. This wasn't bad if you just have a bit of empathy for him, but they really should at least hire a busboy to help out. They had a very simple menu, with only lasagna, spaghetti, meatballs, ravioli, pizza, and sandwiches. The back of the menu said they were famous for their homemade raviolis and pizza. I ordered meat raviolis with meat balls and tried to talk hubby into ordering pizza, but he wanted lasagna. The meal comes with bread and salad. We upgraded to garlic bread for $1 each. Big mistake on the lasagna. There was nothing in it but pasta, and then cheese on top, baked. No cheese or meat in the middle. It had little flavor. My lasagna at home would have gotten 5 stars from Reno if this spot got 4.5 stars. It was so plain, he had to take one of my meatballs. My ravioli came with 2 meatballs, and watery meat sauce. The inside was mushy, and tasted like poor quality meat. The sauce had no flavor to it. The "garlic bread" was just dinner rolls with garlic powder, salt, and butter on it. It was so toasted, it cut up the roof of my mouth. I'm not sure if this is what "authentic" Italian homecooking is like, but if it is, please let me have Macaroni Grill any day! Highlight of the meal is when momma came out of the kitchen and started clearing off some tables. She's really sweet, and comes by the tables to see if you're doing ok. I even got a picture with her as proof! Hubby wants to come back and give the pizza a try. I wouldn't mind either, as I want to support the local mom and pop shops. Plus the spot was CHEAP. The most expensive wine bottle in the place was $10. Corkage was $5. Total meal was under $30.

I felt like I was in the German version of the Fieldhouse. Then again, a place this untrashy is welcome on South Street. text: Copabanana has a couple of outposts in Philly, but the South Street venue is the one that most people think of if you mention Copa. text: The start made me nervous, but the finish was a huge win. I was celebrating a ten year anniversary weekend and had booked this restaurant based on Yelp reviews. When we showed for the reservation we had made, they did not have it in the books, and people were waiting outside. Uh oh. Alas, within moments the owner/manager was all over it. He declared to the hostess that those waiting could wait, we would take precedence and within three minutes we were at a table. A great bounce back from a failure to have our reservation in the books. Next, we order. The menu is just the right length. The waiter knew the specials and shared them effectively, indeed we were tempted to order one of them. I ordered the spaghetti and meatballs. Whenever I try an Italian place for the first time, I like to order this so I can baseline the joint. The answer here was a solid score. The meatball was tender, the pasta cooked to perfection, and the sauce had a perfect tomato acid. The white wine sauce sausage ravioli special was equally if not more amazing. My wife's white wine was the perfect pairing. We were both happy. The ambiance is casual with what looks like a heavy local presence. The bar dominating at least a third of the floor space likely contributes to the locals feels. It is good for people watching. Dress code is relatively casual (khakis and polo shirt for men is safe). The service was good. The pricing was a strong value and the food was excellent. It is on my list of favorites in Santa Barbara. The owner/manager won me over with his bounce back from the failed reservation.

text: This place is next to our local Wawa, and after years of ignoring it we decided to stop here for a quick bite. The menu looked promising and well put together. But the food was absolutely mediocre, and we ordered fairly plain dishes. I'm not a picky eater, and I was hungry enough to eat a full meal, but I ended up picking at my salad (which was fresh-looking but flavorless) and didn't finish my French onion soup...which has never happened before, in the history of my restaurant-hopping. Cheese on top was burnt, tasteless, and rubbery, the soup itself had a strange non-food-like taste. There was something synthetic about all the food--I can only imagine that maybe midwinter food supplies for this restaurant are grown in conditions that aren't conducive to flavor. An example of two of their menu items are things called "Jack Daniels Chicken" and "Tortellini de la Casa". HUH? Come again? Their "Chicken & Shrimp Creole" is some confused mishmosh slop with stale, dried chicken bits and what appear to be Chinese shrimp with one or two whole crawfish which appear to have been laying out on the counter for hours; the food equivalent of multiple personality disorder. Reading their website, the owner decided on the name of the place from an old 1980s movie. Well, might as well since judging from the food and the business model, he has never worked in, lived near nor had the pleasure of enjoying the food of Louisiana or any restaurant with normal business hours and good food. What's most annoying about this place are the hours. The website will tell you they're open from about noon through 1a.m.. However, it took us THREE attempts to eat at this place before we could ever discover it opened. A truly horrible experience not for the serious or casual diner or even those dieing from starvation. Poor focus on maintaining customer trust. The owner needs to shutter the place or sell it off before he embarrasses himself or his family even more. text: This is a relatively new place that opened in the last few weeks to some good reviews. It is located in the renovated historic Superintendent's building right across from Iron Hill Brewery and is owned by Baxters (except that it is not like a typical Baxters). Now on to the food... There were a few interesting sounding things on the menu such as Scallop Tart, Tuna Tower, Lobster Bread Pudding, etc which caught my eye, but since I had heard about the Ratatouille Napolean, I knew what appetizer I wanted before setting eyes on the menu. The presentation and assembly was a little surprising but in a good way (we can use a little more creative thinking in the suburbs). However, the assembly of the dish took away the dept of flavor you get when all the ingredients have been slowly cooking together for hours. Wife got the Wild Mushroom Cannelloni - with roasted tomato sauce and Parmesan whipped goat cheese(?) For our main entrees I got the Earth and Sea special - Hawaiian Snapper roll in a wonton wrapper over Asian salad (had some seaweed in it) and Moroccan spiced lamb over mashed potatoes and spinach. Interesting combination of the Asian and Moroccan styles on the same plate. The snapper roll could have benefited from a touch of salt and the lamb could have been spiced a little bolder. The special was priced at $30, which is on the higher end for dishes in the suburbs and for that people expect better execution of the dishes, similar to Majolica a few blocks down the road or Birchrunville Store Cafe a few miles away. Wife had Shrimp over goat cheese scallion polenta, roasted tomatoes and lemon basil butter. We were glad to see that the shrimp was grilled and the polenta was smooth and creamy. I was a little disappointed when we got a faint tint of amonia from the shrimp. However, since only my palate detected it, we did not send this back, but in retrospect, we probably should have. Dessert was dark chocolate mousse in layered puff pastry (like a Napoleon). It was good, but a pet peeve of mine is powdered sugar sprinkled all over the plate. Overall, food was good and hope they tighten up the execution of the dishes over time, service is friendly and there are few more items on the menu I would like to try, including the "bar menu". Said they would open for lunch probably in early Aug 2008.

They also have a decent selection of bulk foods and even some prepared raw items. The cafe and deli are well stocked with a decent selection of items. text: I'm not telling you anything new by telling you that Whole Foods is expensive -- very expensive for most items. For example, I personally like to examine prices on regular skinless chicken breast when comparing supermarkets. At this Whole Foods location it goes for $6.99 per pound. Let that sink in for a moment. The regular skinless chicken breast I have sitting in my fridge was purchased for $1.99 per pound at the Chinese grocery market at 1012 Cherry Street. Please begin your rant now on: A). Organic B). Locally grown C). Free range D). Growth hormones E). All of the above Finished? Now I'll proceed. Are you kidding me... $6.99 per pound for fucking chicken breast?!? Is this a joke? Or just simply white guilt? I mean, seriously, Wawa and 7-Eleven are cheaper than this store. That being stated, I do agree that quality costs more, and Whole Foods does provide quality products. Quality products and selective price gouging. You can find deals though. Their generic brand, 365 Organic, is comparably priced to other supermarkets. And their staff is generally young, vibrant, and friendly. Additionally, if you like your skinny jeans and ironic mustaches co-mingled with stuffy executive-level refinement, you'll find your fair share here. In all seriousness though, I do appreciate a clean supermarket and an attention to presentation. Whole Foods excels in these qualities. You like cheese? They have a fantastic cheese selection for a grocery store (but you'll pay $$$ for it). The prepared foods (also $$$) are excellent. If I was a squirrel, I would break into this store to feast upon the various assortment of nuts, grains, and all salt of the earth. And the produce section, it's a veggie lover's wet dream. In conclusion, if/when I become sustainably flushed with cash from a renewable source, I will come here every week. Until then, I will continue to only selectively shop at Whole Foods.

text: Ok...so by the looks of my reviews, it appears that I only eat breakfast, but what can I say...I find breakfast/brunch cathartic. Finally one morning I drove past it with a friend and yelled WAIIIIITTTTT! After a quick loop around the block we parked in the lot( yes a parking lot in the city...hooray!) and happily waited only about 5 minutes for a table. I was pleasantly surprised at the lack of a wait on a Saturday morning at 10am. We were seated and promptly greeted by a super cute and friendly waitress with coffee in hand. What more can I ask for with my coffee than a cute girl in awesome boots? Their menu is small, but I appreciate that in a restaurant. To me, this means that they know what they are making and they do it damn good! I had an omelet with avocado and swiss, yummy homefries( the big chunky kind), and probably the second best multi-grain bread in the city(aside from metro). The omelet was a great size and I only ate half. It was priced at 10 dollars which seems about right against comps. The bread is made fresh on premises, as are the pastries. I grabbed a banana muffin to go because they had been staring at me the whole time. It was one of the best muffins I have ever had. It was chock full of bananas that caramelized from baking and they were insanely cake like and indulgent. That thing about only having a 5 minute wait...yeah that quickly changed. As we were nearing the end of our meal the line was starting to go outside and was becoming a 30 minute wait. I have to say though, we were never rushed out. Even after we had received our check and the line was growing, we were offered more coffee. Although we declined in order to free up our table, the offer was really appriciated in this city. The one negative I will mention is that they don't have room for strollers inside and you are asked to leave them outside. There were a few angry parents who were forced to leave their 1000 orbit stroller outside. So word to the wise...grab your sling and strap the kids in. So yeah, don't go to morning glory walk a few blocks east and head to this quaint and lovely cafe.

text: First off it's called Brophy's Brothers. If that doesn't shout a damn good time then I don't know what does. Let's get to the skinny of this. This is a seafood restaurant on the harbor so dammit make sure you eat seafood. This is what we had. Clam Chowder - Nice chunks of clam but watery. I don't think I need to say more. Splash Cafe (see my reviews) hands down. Funny thing is, I ran into a local woman outside that was trying to school us on the food and we were told that the Clam Chowder was the best she had ever had. Let's put it this way I can think of 5 places without even blinking an eye better than this place. Oysters On The Half Shell - Fresh, Cold and Tasty. Horseradish was not very good but other than that you rarely can mess this up with restaurants on the shore. Grilled Salmon Salad - Portions were hearty. I'm talking nice bright colored vegetables, cherry tomatoes, olives etc... I swear it looked like grandma just picked it out of the garden. Calamari - Ok this is where the money was. Damn thing was so good and you know what, it was the best I've ever had. Calamari was tender and juicy and the batter was incredible. It was not that crappy batter they use on onion rings nor was it the thick coating that others use. This was perfectly coated yet thin and flaky. It crumbled in your mouth and was perfectly seasoned. I would go back for this alone. They also had in the same section of fried goodies, clams, scallops, shrimps and fish. I'm just hoping they use the same batter and this is for sure a repeat stop on my next road trip. This place really deserves a 5 but it was hard for me to decide because if the local was telling me the clam chowder was the best she had ever had and claimed to have eaten the whole menu then damn it should be pretty good. The rest of the meal was a 5 but I then think to myself what others things on the menu could be like the clam chowder. Looking around I saw some things that looked ok. I guess I didn't really have a complete meal but their fish selection really looked good. Maybe on my next trip I'll have to try other things on the menu and I can revise my review to a 5.

text: Living in Chicago for only three weeks is already starting to spoil me on the whole vintage thing. Sure, there are a fair number of "vintage" clothing shops here that are overpriced, trying to goad you into buying a western shirt for $30 you could easily get at some other shop for a lot less. While those places are a pain, there are the places here who will actually put stuff on sale, have a lot of sidewalk sales, and who keep prices low. Nashville, on the other hand, suffers from a bad vintage disease. Most of the places in town to buy true vintage stuff double as costume rental places, so they keep a lot of the best stuff aside for costumes, and then overcharge for the stuff that they sell. Sure, vintage brass beltbuckles are cool, but I shouldn't see a $25 price tag on one. And I get that you're in Music City, USA, but only custom made Western shirts are really ever worth more than fifteen bucks. Boomerang, on the other hand, stands tall against the Nashville vintage norm. The prices aren't cheap, but they're not astronomical either, and the stuff being purchased for resale here is obviously quality. The owner is a man of discerning taste, and it shows in the stuff that he has for sale. Not just clothing, but also lots of great kitschy and not so kitschy furniture and housewares. As for the clothing, I've found something almost every time I've walked through the door. If you're into the whole pearl button, Western shirt thing, they tend to be cheaper at Boomerang than most other places, unless you're one of the lucky few who can find them at Southern Thrift or Goodwill. They usually range from $12-$17 here, which in Nashville is not bad at all. The clothing options for women aren't as plentiful as the ones for men, and I've never had a lot of reason to look through them, so I can't comment as much on that selection. But everything in this store is worth a look, so I don't see why the female clothing would be any different. I can't write this without mentioning that the last time I was in there before the big move North, I found the most amazing vintage hat that fit me just perfect. It only cost me $25, which is honestly a great price for a vintage hat in this good of condition. Thanks Nashville, and thank you Boomerang.

text: Our family scoured the area for a good restaurant that we could sit down in and enjoy some hot, fresh Chinese food. Had it not been for a glowing recommendation via word of mouth, we may never have tried this place. Let's face it, something called "The Black Dog Cafe" doesn't exactly scream "Chinese food" to me, it sounded more like a bar for biker gangs. We were a fairly large party of 7. This establishment is not well-suited for large parties (it is not a large place) so we were pretty crammed into our seats. Basically if any of us had to get up, most of us had to get up to let that person out. This was mildly annoying because I never got the sense that I could stretch out or get too comfortable. However, despite this slight inconvenience, the place looked quite clean and I very much appreciated that. What about the food? I ordered the chicken lo mein and a spring roll. First, the servers brought out salads for all of us, which was soon followed by spring rolls, which was soon followed by soups, and finally our entrees. All of the food was absolutely delicious. It was hot, it was fresh, and the taste was exactly what I was hoping for. Everything looked clean and was nicely presented. The food gets an "A". The service was great as well. Great service is really a simple thing. All anyone asks for is a server with a smile, an attention to your needs, and to put your satisfaction first. It's a rare thing these days, but The Black Dog Cafe had all these things. Great service and no BS. I should mention that most orders come with the salad, soup, and entree all as separate courses. This makes the typical dinner meal pretty drawn out. We were in there for two hours total, and though we enjoyed the company and food, there were more than a few times that we were craning our necks in anticipation that our food might soon be rounding the corner. Pricing is reasonable and acceptable based on the quality of food we had. My Chicken Lo Mein dish was $15 at dinner. It was worth every penny. So yeah, it might have taken a while to get through the courses and yes, the facility was a bit small for our party, but in the end it is the food and the service that matters most. The Black Dog Cafe's clean, great-tasting food and attentive service make this an easy recommendation.

text: I can't begin to say enough good things about this restaurant. After sampling their tasty food at the annual International Festival in Tower Grove Park, I decided to pay the restaurant a visit for the whole experience. When you walk in the door, you're immediately met with a wonderful hospitality and graciousness that makes you feel you've stepped into someone's home as a valued guest. It is a large, attractive restaurant perfect for banquets and gatherings, as well as a quiet dinner for two. Bosnian music plays discreetly in the background, and in the winter a huge fireplace crackles and warms the body and spirit. There are white tablecloths and the decor makes you feel you're in the owner's home village. The place is run by family, and it's obvious they take great pride in all that they do. The food is indescribably delicious and the service is amazing!. On 5 different visits, every dish I've had was wonderfully prepared, presented, and tasty. I especially enjoyed the mixed grill, beef goulash (with unbeleivably light spaetzle) , sarma (cabbage rolls), and German chicken kebabs. The homemade soups are to die for. The Grbic salad is a great alternative to the ubiquitous same old Italian salad one finds all over St. Louis. Plenty of fresh bread and your glass is never empty. Last night, the Grbics fulfilled a special request and stayed open past their normal hours for our small post-symphony party. Every detail was perfect and made for an unbelievably magical evening for us! Every member of our party remarked on how lovely the restaurant was and how wonderful the food tasted. The pastries at the end of the meal melted in our mouths, especially the palacinke - Bosnian chocolate filled crepes. I will never forget the Grbic's authentic kindness, generosity, and graciousness - this place is a hidden gem in St. Louis. I VERY highly recommend it.

text: This place has no consistency. I had a great meal here a while back, shortly after it opened, but last Friday night everything was wrong. We got a table outside and both ordered apricot mojitos, and she ordered a shrimp and mushroom dish. I had already eaten. Her dish was brought out almost immediately -- before we even got our drinks -- but it wasn't cooked. It was literally chopped mushrooms and shrimp on a plate and not hot. It was about 15 minutes before a server walked by. My friend pointed out that earlier in the week she had ordered this dish was hot and sauteed. The server apologized and took it away. Meanwhile, we are still waiting for our drinks. Maybe they forgot about us because we were outside? We flagged down another server, who went to get them. At that point we'd been waiting 20 minutes for two cocktails! She served them finally, and I'm sorry, but the apricot mojito was just weird. I drank it all but I didn't enjoy it. A few minutes later, my friend's mushroom and shrimp dish comes out, done correctly this time. I decided to order another drink while she ate, and I ordered a gin and tonic. It was brought out in a tiny glass, around the size of a Dixie cup. My friend called it a "sippy cup" and we laughed and wondered wtf was going on. I don't know what's up with this place, but after being in business for more than two years, you would expect some consistency. It seemed like all the servers were totally confused. There doesn't seem to be any kind of system for taking food and drink orders and bringing them out. While we were there, we were waited on by four or five different people, and all of them seemd like they didn't know what they were doing.

text: I had been wanting to go back to Green Eggs for brunch since I had stopped by a few months ago. Based on the croissant I had tried that day, I was concerned the food would just be MEH, and after our brunch visit, I'm not convinced it wasn't. Was that too many double negatives? Heh, I guess you could say, I'm undecided about this place, and I most definitely wasn't blown away. WHAT WE ATE *Breakfast Burrito: On the menu, they actually list all of the MANY ingredients that are in the burrito and I was very excited about this. It sounded hearty and I thought the olives and corn would be nice additions. What they don't tell you is that the "signature potato" includes huge pieces of red and green bell peppers. Which, in my hatred of that wretched vegetable, immediately makes me go EWWWWWW. Okay okay okay, I know that not many people agree with the EWWW assessment of bell peppers, but whatever your take on it is, it's undeniably a strong and very distinctive flavor. So, I'm sure for those folks that LIKE them, they add great flavor dimensions to dishes, but for those of us that really have a strong aversion to them, it taints the entire dish. ESPECIALLY, when they sneak up on you, like they did in the breakfast burritos. And, btw, the signature potatoes are in other dishes as well, so diner beware. I want to say that if it hadn't been for the bell pepper sneak attack, I would have enjoyed this more. But then again, P didn't really love it either and he digs bell peppers. *The kitchen sink If I had to break this down, I'd say the presentation definitely rocks, but the food itself was okay. The eggs and cheese part were pretty yummy - well cooked, but once again, the bell pepper factor in the potato mixture came into play here. JJP hates bell peppers as much as I do, so again, too much sneak attack pepper taste. The sausage pieces were great. If anything, I wished there were a bit more of them throughout - but hey, isn't that always true? The biscuits weren't buttery at all, so my guess is they bake these on-site just for this particular dish. Probs dry alone, but as part of this particular dish, they were really good. The REASON they were really good, however, is because of the decadent, creamy, savory sausage gravy..... mmmmmmmmmmmmmmm. The three of us were scooping this gravy up like it was soup. Wow, I realize that sounds gross, but it was really so good. Super rich, but not overly salty or overwhelmingly heavy. Without a doubt, this gravy makes/saves this dish. *Stone Ground Grits The grits were cooked well enough, but was too cheese heavy. It is surprising that I say that, but I would guess they used shredded cheddar mixed into the grits, and the result was that it thickened the grits too much. The grits, while they tasted okay, were too dense and thick and piece-y - almost lumpy - and that's not what you want. At least, that's not what I want.

text: Oh, 50 Flowers. So I'd read a lot online about DIYing wedding flowers, and that 50Flowers' prices were really great. My now sister-in-law wasn't too jazzed about using flowers as centerpieces at her wedding, but my Mom was pretty intent on having at least SOMETHING on the tables. So we settled on getting a load of premium gerber daisies ordered from 50flowers.com and would just put 5 stems in each table's vase for some color. We ordered some white ones and some tinted green ones. I'm talking like, 4 months in advance. We followed all of their directions--Ordered for Thursday delivery for their Saturday wedding. So you can imagine our surprise when my Mom received the flowers that Thursday before the wedding. And there were white daisies and RED DAISIES. Not a green one in sight. Yeah. Not what we ordered. Especially when we're wearing KELLY GREEN BRIDESMAID DRESSES and all accents at the wedding were kelly green. Red. OMG. HELLO CHRISTMAS. Now most brides would have lost their mind, and 50Flowers was lucky that I was NOT the bride in this instance. I called them immediately and let them know what we received. They told me they'd been waiting for my call, as the bride who HAD received my green daisies had already called them. They didn't know WHO received her red ones. Turned out it was me. So yeah. TWO unhappy customers right there. Apparently they can't get the right flowers in the right boxes. I was then told that there wasn't any way we could get the correct green daisies by Saturday. Something about them needing time to tint. Great. She told me she could get me some more white ones, though. I opted not to. Frankly, I didn't want to end up in the same scenario on the day of the wedding. I asked for a full refund for all of the green daisies we never received. They obliged and said the refund would process to my credit card within 3-5 business days. That's when I got on the phone with some other awesome local flower shops, told them my scenario, and decided to order some daisies from them. Visser's Florist in Anaheim saved my day--getting me 75 AWESOME white gerber daisies the next morning for just 10 cents more per stem. But let's talk about the quality of the daisies we received from 50Flowers. This was the ONE thing I was worried about. Their pictures are awesome. And then the packaging was seemingly awesome, too. Each daisy came with a plastic stem holder, along with some netting around each flower, so the petals wouldn't break or fall off. We immediately put the daisies in water when we received them. Kept them inside, out of the sun, and changed their water the next morning to keep the bacteria out. The flower seemed small for a gerber--probably about 3.5 inches? When I think of "premium" (which is what they called these), this isn't what I picture. Saturday rolled around, and the white daisies looked AWFUL. Especially compared to the 75 white daisies I'd ordered from Visser's. They looked tiny (the ones from Visser's were at least 5 inches diameter--some bigger), and were completely wilting. Comparatively, they weren't even in the same league as the daisies I'd gotten from Visser's. We truly didn't know what to do with them. We used them in some of the smaller vases, but they ended up being a big waste, since we had to toss so many of them because they either lost tons of petals or were drooping to the point of no return. For some bizarre reason, the red daisies held up much better. Not that that helped us, since we had no use for them. They sat at my Mom's house in a vase. It's now been 10 days since I've asked for my refund (8 business days) and I still don't see it processed to my credit card statement. I e-mailed their customer service dept. about this on Friday, but still haven't heard back. I'll be checking everyday, and will be disputing it with my credit card company if they don't get it processed this week. I'll update about that when it happens. Definitely wouldn't recommend them. This isn't the sort of stress a bride wants to deal with two days before her wedding. Their nonchalant attitude was pretty offputting as well. I understand that quality sometimes differs from flower to flower, but sending you the wrong thing just isn't acceptable. ETA: Just wanted to update about my refund to my credit card. They sent me an e-mail regarding the refund on Monday, August 30, however, it didn't post to my account until Wednesday, September 1. I'm assuming that's how long it takes a refund to post, but I received the wrong flowers on August 19th. Seems like an awful long time to hold onto someone's money, especially when there was never even a dispute about what had happened.
label: NEG

text: I live about 3 blocks west of this place and as convenient as that is I can't bring myself to go there anymore. But first I will tell you the positives... First off, I appreciate a well-crafted beer as much as anyone but all of their high-gravity beers give me an immediate headache and I've been drinking all kinds of beer for 20+ years. As a matter of fact, when I was a youth I used to make the trek from Jersey up to the old Dock St. with friends (because it was the only place that wouldn't card us). Second, any restaurant that has exceptional food but lacks quality service - or vice versa - that leaves even one customer saying, "maybe it would be better next time" fails, in my humble opinion. And in this instance, I don't care how tasty the fig pizza might be, when servers take jobs at popular gathering places as a means to boast their own achievements and wait on their own friends, more so than to bring me said fig pizza when it's actually hot, they have failed to represent the establishment as a reputable one. There's nothing worse than listening to some girl in a neckerchief and no bra talk about how awesome her llama tour across Mongolia was to her friends that are paying in nickels when you can see your food getting cold behind her. Basically V8 and a little vodka in the glass. text: As I mentioned in my review of the Sheraton, I needed a place to watch the England vs. Algeria World Cup game while my lovely wife shopped with her daughter and grandkids. We timed our trip down there perfectly and I was sitting at the bar with time to spare! There were lots of TVs in this place and they had music playing that gave the bar a very cool vibe to it. I came to learn that Ernesto, the bartender, was very cool. He greeted me right away and wanted to get me set up as best as humanly possible. I picked my best vantage point and while I wasn't all that hungry, looked over the menu. Everything looked and sounded tasty, but I was in game mode and all I really wanted was a GOOD Bloody Maria. Long ago I accepted the fact that not all bars make good Bloody Marys/Marias. Would I be as lucky today as the US was against England in their first game of the World Cup or would I be victimized like we were in the Slovenian match? Ernesto was fired up to make me one and I was buoyed by his enthusiasm. It took a few minutes and when he was done, I have to say Ernesto has Fire + Spice in the plus column! My Bloody was so good I had to tell myself to slow down and savor it... I didn't want to be wasted by the time the Mrs. showed up. While England looked very uninspired during their match against Algeria, Ernesto & Co. were taking up the slack. People started to filter in for lunch, but I was the only one at the bar. Even though he started to get busy with orders for the lunch crowd he made sure to take care of me. Ernesto set out some very spicy chex mix for me. This mouth charring, endorphin pumping variant did not come out of a Chex Mix bag. It was "this is freakin' hot but I can't stop eating it" good. I meant to ask where it came from, but again I was in game mode and Ernesto could sense it. He was friendly, but not disruptive (and ended up giving me the remote so I could turn the volume up). He poured me a Dos Equis and kept tabs on me. At half time, I ordered a Sonoran Quesadilla. Not because I was super hungry, but it just looked so good: Roasted poblano's, oaxaca cheese, salsa fresca,crema ...for a buck they add beef machaca and it rolled out at $8. It came with salsa but it was so tasty, I didn't want to spoil it in any fashion. I wished I would have been starving, because I wanted to try a whole lot more on the menu. Anyway, the second half came and went uneventfully. England failed to produce, yet Ernesto & Fire + Spice came up big! I settled my tab and told Ernesto I would be back for a margarita to take back poolside. Everyone claims they have good margs...if life was only that simple. I tried two, just to make sure! They were as good as he claimed they were going to be. I wasn't completely bombed when the Mrs. returned. She tried to catch up and pitched in an order of cherry vodka & soda water. She tried two ..they tasted like cherry vodka & soda water. LOL! Our last report is on breakfast. We mosied on down there for breakfast thinking our breakfast vouchers were going to be for some prepacked bagels or honey buns and maybe a small carton of milk or Donald Duck OJ. The waitress informed us that they were good for the All- American breakfast. Mrs. asked if we could substitute it for the Breakfast Burrito..she is so good at that! They hooked us up and we both enjoyed one of the best breakfast burritos ever. It is not a humongous stomach stretching burrito, but a respectfully sized burrito. Some say that it is not the size of your burrito that matters , but what is inside. I believe it...in this case. Not only was the burrito delish....the hash browns were some of the best tasting shredded spuds we have ever had. The Mrs. couldn't finish hers and I was too full to help out. Guess it was big enough! The Sheraton is lucky to have this place on the property! I would go there even if I wasn't staying at the hotel.

text: I didn't sit at the swings at the bar. I think for a lightweight like myself, swinging and drinking is a dangerous combination, but if you can handle it, it looks like it could be fun--or motion-sickness inducing... I loved our server. She was cute and sweet and efficient, just the right mix of not in our faces but not inattentive. I liked my drinks, but would advise key lime martini fans to avoid this one--it's just not quite right. The raspberry fizzy thing was good, though. :) Our party of six sampled a few tapas and they were hit or miss, I thought. I loved the crispy hearts of palm with soffrito aioli (it's fried with aioli! What's not to love??), thought the New Orleans-style BBQ shrimp was tasty (although I couldn't figure out what, exactly, was Nawlins 'bout 'em) and did not enjoy the plantain tostones with goat cheese. They just didn't taste like much to me, which is sorta surprising given the goat cheese and its pairing with roasted pepper mojo. For my entree, I chose the pan-seared scallops special with yucca mashed potatoes and green beans and left nary a bite on my plate. The scallops were good-sized and nicely seared and while there wasn't anything totally unique or amazing about the sides, they were definitely tasty. I'm not really sure what the red oily sauce was that surrounded everything, but I was able to avoid most of it, so no worries there. Justin loved his ropa vieja, but I thought it was very barbecued beef-Mamwich-flavored and not quite what I expected. His sister had the paella, which we all enjoyed, but if you're not a bean lover, steer clear--there's more than a few of 'em in here. I didn't try anyone else's dishes, but there were few leftovers to cart home, so that's a good sign. Those who know me know that I'm a dessert junkie. Even if I'm bursting at the seams, I often order dessert, at least to share (and then I usually eat more than my fair share of it, even if it means I'm rolled out of the restaurant with a major belly ache). This night was no different and we ordered the brioche bread pudding to share. Like I said, I usually eat more than I should, but this bread pudding just wasn't doin' it for me. One bite was plenty and sadly forgettable. The good part about that was it meant I didn't totally overdo it. :) I'd put Boogaloo at 3.5 stars right now. It wasn't outstanding, it wasn't great, but it was definitely *pretty* great. I loved the atmosphere, our server and some of our food, and I see from other folks that some dishes and some nights are better than others. I'd be happy to head back and try more of their offerings. Although I'm still gonna pass on the swings. Now pass me the crispy hearts of palm, already!

text: I've always considered myself to be better than homeless people. The list of my superiorities is so extensive that I almost don't even know where to start. My style is more sophisticated, my palate is more refined, my book collection is more impressive, my hygiene is far superior, and, most obviously, I have an actual home. Last Friday, as I was leap-frogging over a bum who had the gall to lay lengthwise across the sidewalk, I found myself marveling at the extreme disparity between my fabulousness and his patheticness. How could two of God's children, cut from the same cloth, be so damn different? I'm generally not one for comparative analysis, but let's call a spade a spade. It's fairly evident that I'm far more advanced than my shoeless brethren and, as a result, I've never found us to have much in common. Well, that's all changed with the arrival of this lovely Spring weather. Turns out, we share a deep-seated passion for one of the greatest hobbies ever invented. Drinking in the park. I love it. For my life, it doesn't get any better than to gather with friends in Rittenhouse to drink beers out of paper cups, catch some rays, and have some laughs. This has gradually become something of a Sunday tradition. There's literally no greater way to reclaim the weekend and ensure maximum utilization of your meager 48 hours of freedom. When we're hankering for cold, crisp brews in the park on a warm, sunny day, we always go to Food and Friends to select from their spectacular collection of beers. While the options tend to run on the pricey side, it's all well worth it. As the gray-heads are wont to say, you get what you pay for. While I don't mind spending nearly $4 for a Flying Dog Double Dog Double Pale Ale (11.4% ABV), it does render the price of a six pack exorbitant and I understand that most people don't want to lace it out in this fashion. Given the downtrodden state of our economy, I know that everyone's looking for a deal and, in my opinion, the best buy currently running at Food and Friends is Old Dominion's Spring Buck Blonde Ale. With 7.8% ABV, tremendous taste, and a price tag of a mere $2.19 per bottle, you can't beat it. So despite my initial speculation, it would appear that I do share something with the shiftless lay-abouts running rampant in Rittenhouse. And while I may opt for the North Coast Brewing Company's Pranqster Belgian Style Golden Ale (7.6% ABV) instead of a plastic pint of Bankers' Club, our intent is clearly the same...to enjoy the weather, take the edge off, and bask in the heart-warming glow of our fellow man.

text: Now this will be the review that puts all these other reviews to shame.....or at least clarifies them a bit. Basically, pretty much every review and rating on here is right. Some nights this place feels like the precious gem it is, other nights just an indistinguishable overpriced bar. So first off I'll give practical advice, get a crepe beforehand and drink downstairs beforehand. They food is good and the drinks are cheaper there, plus you don't have to pay cover to go upstairs if you get food. But they only charge on the weekends anyway. Still, a crepe is a crepe.... The decor is french cabaret, very nice, very clean place, so at least your hands are always guaranteed clean if you use the restroom there (assuming of course you choose to wash them...). Night to night though, the crowd an the offering change, dramatically at that. One night they may do a burlesque show, so you'll be surrounded by faux intellectual hipsters that find everything "marvelous." It still fun though. Another night, it'll be a whole crown dressed in 1940s attire doing the tango. These are probably the best nights. And then another night, it's the same deafening music you can get anywhere else in a too crowded place. So I take off a star for that. And that's what I think all the negative reviews here represent. Ironically enough, these are the most crowded nights to be there. So that's my review, it's a schizophrenic lounge kind of place that doesn't know what it is, but it's still one of my favorites.
label: POS

text: The Missouri Bar & Grille--basically, on the corner of Tucker and Washington--is below average food at an above average price (if any ad shops around town want to use my clever and original slogans and catch-alls, such as the one above, contact me via my Yelp™ account). The best thing about MoBar is their kitchen's hours of operation--open until 2:30 in the mornin', 365 days a year. No matter how bad the food, I will always applaud a place that serves options other then omlettes and sliders at odd hours of the night. Throw in the fact that I can also get a drink at said institution, and you've just earned yourself another star. That being said, thank god I have that rule, because MoBar's food isn't so hot. The cheeseburger that the lady friend ordered was okay, but I don't really know if you can truly fuck up a cheeseburger. Perfecting it is another story, but it's definitely near impossible to fuck it up. Another friend and I ordered the gyro and fries. I know, ordering a gyro at a American dive bar is akin to buying apple pie at a cricket match, but I figured, "hell, it's on the menu, and who knows, maybe the owner is Greek." The owner isn't Greek. MoBar is definitely a dive that knows it's a dive. The place literally looks like they just threw shit in some rooms and said, "fuck it, tap the kegs." Whoever put up their dart boards has poor spacial reasoning skills, because it's right beside the door--meaning that whoever is walking in, walks right in the flight path. Their side room, which I assume is the "restaurant side" during the day, was filled with what looked like brass-laden buffet bars that were back lit, giving off this scary as shit vibe, like I was in a haunted Ponderosa. When I asked if they had any drink specials, the 60-something Winston smoking barkeep, looked at me and deadpanned, "everything I make is special." Fantastic. Overall, this place is only worth going if you're downtown and want something to eat after everything else has closed. And you're drunk. And can't drive to Sandrina's. And you want to get hit with a dart. Okay, I kid; the food is, eh, but honestly, the quality of food that was coming out of the kitchen, at that price (the menu is deceptive, in that many items are a la carte--prices range from $6-$15), isn't worth going to for anything other than if you're drunk and just want a steak, no matter how bad. If that's what you want though, five stars!

You can happily avoid the typical gringo/Mexican chimichangas, fajitas, burros, taco salads and hamburger tacos you find at most Tucson restaurants. Instead you can get machaca, pozole, menudo, huevos con nopalitos, picadillo, chilaquiles and other not-smothered-with-lettuce-and-kraft-cheese food. It may not be healthy, but for sure tastes good and is real Mexican food. Call it ethnic comfort food. Lunch buffet was very tasty with lots of choices, under $8 per humanoid including drinks.
